body: Reviewed /converge (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, prompts/fix.md, verify.md, owner-list.md, scripts/review fixes/verifies/drives, scripts/tasks close) for the whole variant: find each break by a drive, then fix it or report it. Then ran the loop's verbs in a scratch project (stack run run-fcb308601e42, trued up from the working tree): one drive failure merged as defect i2, review fixes --round 1 filed fix task t4 with --mark fixing, the fixer closed t4 'done' (--staged tool.sh --sites tool.sh) without running tasks item set on i2. The story promises: each break the check finds is fixed, so a change that breaks a promise does not reach users unnoticed. Saw: tasks close accepts a done close of a batch fix task whose defect still stands 'fixing' (cmd_close checks only swept-role --sites); i2 stayed 'fixing'; review verifies --snapshot fix-1.json printed {"verify_tasks": []} because cmd_verifies takes only fixed/declined/duplicate; tasks item list --state open printed []; review drives --confirm --dry-run printed {"pending": []}. So Loop 2 step 2 ('Where no defect stands at open, the loop ends') ends the loop with the break neither fixed nor verified. SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 resets defects 'still fixing' only after a partial/blocked/disputed close ('A fix task that closes blocked or disputed, or partial with any other result, is refiled once ... its defects still fixing go back to open'), never after a done close. owner-list.md reads only 'the defects stuck, the defects still open or fixed where the run ended before they were verified, the defects at declined or duplicate with no verified field' and never names 'fixing', and the return's 'fixed' line counts verified, declined, duplicate, and stuck. The found break therefore reaches neither the fix loop, the intake, nor the report: it goes unnoticed, against the story's 'have each break that check finds fixed, so that a change that breaks a promise does not reach my users unnoticed' and decision converge-finds-then-fixes ('Every defect on the list is fixed in the run, declined with a reason a verifier accepts, or stuck', SKILL.md 'The intent is to fix, not to file').

What I did, in order: in a scratch project (stack run run-0a5e9cb47566, git init), ran true-up (exit 0), resolve citation-tags, wire-hooks lint (wired: PostToolUse matcher "" running node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.ok-planner/hooks/post-edit.js"), committed a base, then fed the wired command Claude Code PostToolUse payloads. Edit, Write, and MultiEdit payloads are checked as promised: a prose comment blocks (exit 2, 'plumbline/comment-hygiene: comment is not permitted'), a test file blocks ('plumbline/no-tests'), an unresolved @practice: slug blocks ('plumbline/citation-unresolved'), legacy debt on unchanged lines of a tracked file passes, each lint_checks switch turned off stops its check and true-up drops the matching rule text, and a declared folder beside the root is checked. Then the gap: an agent edit made through the Bash tool is never checked. With src/edit-time-lint-bash.js holding 'export const y = 2; // bash-written residue' on disk, a realistic Bash payload {tool_name:Bash, tool_input:{command:'printf ... > src/edit-time-lint-bash.js'}} gave 'hook exit=0' and no output, while the same file under a Write payload gave exit 2 with the comment-hygiene violation. A NotebookEdit payload on src/edit-time-lint.ipynb whose cell holds '# this sets x to one' also gave 'hook exit=0', and 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/edit-time-lint.ipynb' exits 0 on it, so notebook edits land unchecked too. The story promises: 'every agent edit checked against the lint checks my project turned on as it lands, so that residue never accumulates.' Saw: only edits through the Edit/Write/MultiEdit tools are checked; an agent that edits with sed -i, a heredoc, a redirect, or a script through Bash (which Claude Code's auto mode tells agents they may do for small edits) lands residue the hook never sees, and it accumulates until a whole-tree lint run. The product says so itself: .claude/rules/plumbline-cheatsheet.md, 'It does nothing for a Bash call.', and decision edit-hook-blocks-in-turn scopes the hook to 'the edited file', so the fix may need the owner's ruling (for example, lint the files git reports changed after a Bash call). Side observation, same hook: the hook also lints on a Read payload, so reading an untracked file that holds a comment gives exit 2 ('src/edit-time-lint-bash.js:1: plumbline/comment-hygiene') on a file the agent did not edit. Evidence: 'hook exit=0' for the Bash and NotebookEdit payloads above; 'hook exit=2' for the Write and Read payloads on the same file.

body: Reviewed /plan-docs (skills/plan-docs/SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) and drove .ok-planner/bin/docs in a scratch project. A docspec's ## Reader and ## Covers (whom the documentation is for, what it tells and leaves out) never cause an edit. {{DOC-EDIT-RULES}} in core.md lists six rules (false claim, missing public element, internal element shown, a closed sprint changed what a user can do through the references, departure from ## Shape or the ## Where layout, unsettleable claim) and then says 'Every other sentence stays as written.' No rule fires when the documentation's reader or coverage departs from ## Reader or ## Covers. Scratch drive: stamped docspec:guides over docs/guides/greet-someone.md, then amended its Reader to 'A person new to the command line who has never run a Python script.' and its Covers to add 'how to install Python first', committed. 'docs window --json' gave status reached, reasons ['docspec changed: .ok-planner/docspec/guides.md'], sprints [], stale_claims 0. Under {{DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT}} steps 1-2 no rule fires and the file is neither changed nor checked ('Any other file is not an item'), so plan-docs step 5 writes 'No item: nothing its reader sees changed.' and the stamp moves past the amendment: the owner's new reader and coverage are never written. The same holds when a docspec is first declared over existing documentation (planner step 3: existing files are change or check 'under the steps above'), so existing text that covers what Covers leaves out, or omits what it names, stays. The style pass also may 'add no claim, and cut none' and revises against Shape, example, and writing standard only. The story promises: 'declare each kind of documentation my project keeps, whom it is for, and what it describes, so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; concept:docspec Purpose: 'The docspec also tells the writer whom the text is for, what to cover, what to leave out ... so the text follows the owner's intent instead of the writer's guess.'; decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window: 'Planning takes each docspec whose own text ... changed since its stamp'. Saw: the window takes the changed docspec text, but no edit rule acts on it.

body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree, declared docspec:api with '## Where' 'in code: `src/tool.py`, `src/tool.ts`', ran catalog-toc (index row: '- `api` — where: in code: `src/tool.py`, `src/tool.ts`; references: `src/tool.py`'), then linted files outside it. 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/other.ts' with '/** Help. */' before an exported function: exit 2, 'plumbline/comment-hygiene: comment is not permitted (... not a doc comment in a file an in-code docspec or a committed earlier marker covers)', as owed; src/tool.ts with the same comment: exit 0, as owed. But 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/other.py', a file no docspec names, holding 'def helper():' with the docstring '"""Help."""': exit 0, no violation. A '# this does a thing' comment in a Python file is refused (exit 2), so the check runs on .py files; a docstring passes because the '.py' grammar treats quoted text as strings. The story promises: a declared kind of documentation is what writers write ('so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'); the docspec definition says 'The lint allows a doc comment on a declaration only in a file an `in code:` line names'. Saw: in Python, doc comments on declarations land in any file, declared or not, and the lint passes them.

In a scratch project (stack run, names set under scratch XDG_CONFIG_HOME): filed and routed issue discuss-an-issue-526f99f3-cli; as Ana ran 'issues comment <id> --text "Why hourly and not on every edit? Does anything else write the cache?"' (message 1, not yet seen, waiting true, unseen 1); wrote triage's answer with 'issues respond' (reply 2 to 1, update 3 of options, seen [1]); then as Ana ran 'issues edit <id> 1 --text "...Does the import job write the cache too, and how often does it run?"' (exit 0, 'triage will see it again'); then 'issues show <id>'. Second issue discuss-an-issue-526f99f3-web: comment answered by a reply, then edited and removed through the dashboard (POST /message/1/edit, /message/1/remove -> {"withdrawn": true}), then 'issues show <id>'. The story promises: a person questions an issue's analysis and gets an answer on that issue, readable so they can rule; decision owner-messages-can-change: 'A message an answer already followed keeps its earlier text beside the change ... Keeping the earlier text of an answered message keeps each reply readable against what it answered.' Saw: 'issues show' prints only the current text of an edited message, with no 'edited' mark and no earlier text, so reply 2 ('Hourly bounds staleness ... the import job also writes the cache') sits under a question it never answered; and a withdrawn message prints as '1. Ana Discuss comment 2026-10-22T10:08:16Z, not yet seen' with its text and no 'withdrawn' mark. Evidence: 'issues show discuss-an-issue-526f99f3-cli' Discussion: '1. Ana Discuss comment 2026-10-22T10:07:14Z, not yet seen / Why hourly and not on every edit? Does the import job write the cache too, and how often does it run? / 2. triage reply to 1 ...'; 'issues show --json' of the same record holds "earlier": ["Why hourly and not on every edit? Does anything else write the cache?"], "edited": "2026-10-22T10:07:41Z"; for the web record --json holds "withdrawn": "2026-10-22T10:09:10Z" while text show says 'not yet seen'. The dashboard page renders 'edited ...', 'withdrawn ...', and 'earlier text (1)' for the same records, so only the CLI's text show drops them. The base flow (comment, answer via respond, rule with 'issues rule') worked.

Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/triage-issues/SKILL.md phase 3 and prompts/respond.md. respond.md Read step 1: 'Every record your task names, whole: .ok-planner/bin/issues show <id> prints its fields, ... and its whole discussion, each message numbered, each person's message seen or not yet seen.' Its Judge step then rests on fields that output never prints: 'A message carrying edited is one you answered before, which its author has since rewritten; its earlier field holds the texts you answered, so answer what changed. A message carrying withdrawn is one its author took back; act on nothing it says.' Run in a scratch project: after an answered comment was edited, 'issues show <id>' printed '1. Ana Discuss comment 2026-10-22T10:07:14Z, not yet seen' with the new text only, no edited mark and no earlier text; after an answered comment was withdrawn, 'issues show <id>' printed it as 'not yet seen' with its text and no withdrawn mark ('issues show --json' holds earlier, edited, and withdrawn). The story promises the person gets an answer on the issue to the question they asked; decision triage-answers-owner-messages: 'A message its author changes after triage saw it waits for the next run again, and a message its author withdraws needs no answer.' A respond agent that reads as the prompt says cannot tell an edited question from a new one, cannot answer what changed, and on a record in scope for another message would answer a withdrawn one as unseen. Fix either the prompt (read with 'issues show <id> --json') or the show output the prompt names.

body: Reviewed the sprint-certification path: /converge sprint, the sprint boilerplate (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md steps 12-13 and the Completion contract), and the scripts it calls (review deltas, review certified). The delta form in skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md {{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}} says: 'Long bodies go in a sidecar, one file per artifact, and the sprint heading reads `body: in the sidecar`'. fix.md and verify.md repeat 'where the heading reads `body: in the sidecar`'. But scripts/review DELTA_HEADING is r'^### (New|Amend|Retire) (?:(concept|story|decision|subject|practice|docspec): (\S+)|surface intent)\s*$', so it only matches a heading that ends at the slug. A heading that carries the pointer, as the form's words say, is not matched, and sprint_deltas() drops that delta without comparing it. Story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint'; decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository: 'One command, `review certified`, checks the contract's items in the repository'; completion contract item 1: 'Every corpus matches every delta above'. Saw: in a scratch project, a sprint with '### New story: cc-sidecar-a — body: in the sidecar' (sidecar file present, artifact never landed), '### New story: cc-sidecar-b' with the line 'body: in the sidecar' under it, and one inline delta. review deltas printed '"compared": 2' and listed nothing for cc-sidecar-a. The certified line 'item 1 (deltas): holds: <n> deltas landed' counts only the parsed deltas. So an approved delta that never landed passes item 1, and the return's deltas line ('<n> compared') undercounts.

Reviewed the sprint-certification path, as in the sibling failure. scripts/review inline_body() opens the delta body at the first line matching '^(`{3,})markdown' and ends it at the first later line equal to that same fence. The delta form ({{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}} in skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md) and the sprint template (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md) say nothing about fencing a body that holds its own code block. So a final-form body that holds a ``` code block, such as a decision that shows a command, is cut short at its first inner fence. Story promises: 'done means the same thing for every sprint'; completion contract item 1: 'Every corpus matches every delta above, applied verbatim'; decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository: certified 'prints SPRINT COMPLETE or SPRINT NOT COMPLETE'. Saw: in a scratch project, the delta '### New decision: cc-fenced' carried a ```markdown body that held '```' / 'make check' / '```'. I copied the whole body into .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md, byte for byte, and regenerated the TOCs. review deltas printed 'unsettled': 'cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body', and review certified printed 'item 1 (deltas): fails' and 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE ... - New decision: cc-fenced: .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body'. A C3 fixer that copies the same body verbatim cannot clear it. A sprint whose delta holds a code block never certifies complete, even though it landed as approved.

In a scratch project (stack up, true-up, git init), I built an approved sprint, a base file, a landed delta, and a converge ledger holding a review task closed done, a drive task, and defects. Then I ran .ok-planner/bin/review approved / certified / deltas through each state. Each of these held: a draft with no mark is refused and named; no completion report fails; an open defect fails; an unlisted stuck defect fails; a listed one passes; a check failing on a changed file fails; a ledger with no drive fails, naming the unfilled drive commands; an archived sprint is found from its sprints/ path; and 'closed:' is terminal. Two parses diverge from the delta form, so 'done' depends on how a delta is written. (1) A heading that carries the sidecar pointer, as {{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}} words it ('the sprint heading reads `body: in the sidecar`'), e.g. '### New story: cc-sidecar-a — body: in the sidecar', is silently skipped. review deltas printed '"compared": 2' for three deltas, and the delta that never landed went unreported. (2) A ```markdown body holding an inner ``` fence is truncated. A verbatim-landed .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md gave 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE ... - New decision: cc-fenced: .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body'. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint'. Saw: certified passes an unlanded delta in case (1) and refuses a landed one in case (2).

body: Reviewed /discover-design (SKILL.md, core.md, scripts/discover) and ran its steps by hand in a scratch project trued up from the working tree, with an empty corpus (no .ok-planner/design/), a 22-line app/ledger.py, and a README: status, tasks init, prompt register, config set item_states, discover areas, discover surveys, survey items, sort and merge per kind, a review cycle with one finding, refile, assemble --check, assemble. The deltas-only path works: the assembled discovery listed 2 promise changes and wrote nothing under .ok-planner/design/. Then, in a copy of that scratch project, I had the story merge record a question instead of a new delta, because the README and the code disagree (the survey prompt, core.md:105, says 'Where prose and code in your area disagree, record the candidate once and say both in its body'). The question used artifact=story:read-balance, stale_op=new, stale_target=story:read-balance, and its answer body sat at answers/void-counting/stories/read-balance.md. The assembly refused it: 'the discovery does not hold: - question void-counting (item i14, task t16): artifact story:read-balance does not exist', exit 2. question_failures in scripts/discover (lines 455-459) requires the question's artifact to be a live file. So on an empty corpus the audit cannot ask any question, and a disagreement the code does not settle can only be dropped or quietly decided as a new delta. That contradicts the review prompt, core.md:513-515: 'Every promise change says what in the code settles it, and the code says it. A promise change the code does not settle is a question.' On an empty corpus every promise change is a new delta, so a reviewer following that line produces a finding that the merge cannot record in a form the assembly accepts. The same gap hits any new artifact on an out-of-date corpus; see the out-of-date failure. The story promises: 'have my existing code read against my design corpus, whether the corpus is empty or out of date, and turned into the corpus changes it needs plus the questions only I can answer'. The decision corpus-audit-hands-a-discovery-to-planning promises: 'It drafts each corpus delta the code and the rules settle, and each question only the owner can answer, with both answers'. Saw: on an empty corpus a discovery can carry deltas and calls but no question. Evidence: the assemble --check output quoted above.

body: Ran /discover-design's steps by hand in a scratch copy holding an out-of-date corpus: concept ledger-entry with a ## History section, and story read-balance, which says voided entries are counted while app/ledger.py skips them. The steps were survey, check (artifacts batched by kind), sort and merge per kind, review, and assemble. The main path holds: the discovery listed one form-only amendment (the History section stripped) and one question with both answers (stale: amend story:read-balance, body under answers/void-counting/; wrong: make balance count voided entries). Nothing under .ok-planner/design/ changed. The gap: the merge prompt, core.md:370, says 'A group under a proposed slug is a gap: where the definitions admit it, it becomes a new delta, marked promise'. That gives a gap only two exits, a new delta or a drop. The review prompt, core.md:513-515, says 'A promise change the code does not settle is a question'. But the assembly's question_failures (scripts/discover:455-459) refuses a question whose artifact is not a live file: 'artifact <kind:slug> does not exist'. So where the code holds something no artifact records (one of the three ways DISCOVER-FINDING-FORMS says a corpus is out of date) and the code and its prose disagree on what it should do, the audit cannot ask the owner. It must decide in a new delta or drop the candidate. This is the same root cause as the empty-corpus failure, here limited to new artifacts. The story promises: 'turned into the corpus changes it needs plus the questions only I can answer'. Saw: questions are possible only on live artifacts. Evidence: the refusal quoted in the empty-corpus failure, which was reproduced with stale_op=new.

body: R4/C2 under A2 (and A9). Trigger: an open category: defect issue whose problem names an absolute extensionless path, such as a shebang '#!/usr/bin/env python3', '/bin/sh', or the port registry's '/etc/services' that .ok-planner/review/project.md itself names. Path: scripts/review:cmd_backlog -> scripts/review:backlog_entry -> PATH_PATTERN (PATH_ALTERNATIVES, line 1027: r'[\w.-]*(?:/[\w.-]+)+|[\w./-]+\.\w+'). The new first alternative matches '/usr/bin/env' (an empty prefix, then '/usr', '/bin', '/env'); backlog_entry then tests os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, token)), and os.path.join with an absolute token returns the token itself, so '/usr/bin/env' passes as a file. left_alone('/usr/bin/env') finds no owner path, no harness match, and no suite stamp in the binary's text, so it returns None, and the token lands in files (line 1084: files.append(token)). Harm: the backlog report's files, and through review fixes the fix task's --files, name a system file outside the project tree as a file the run may edit (a write target the run should never reach); an issue that names only such a path and no project file now yields a report with site '/usr/bin/env' instead of going under settled, so the report says the issue names a file of the tree. Scope: caused by the change. The base PATH_PATTERN r'[\w./-]+\.\w+' required an extension, so extensionless absolute paths such as /usr/bin/env, /bin/sh, and /etc/services never matched; absolute paths with an extension stood at the base the same way. B9 lists the widening only for paths inside the tree ('an issue naming only an extensionless file' of the tree).

body: Build call i15 (t13) left a harm. Rule: .ok-planner/docs/events.md 'Where the code emits': 'every error caught: a catch that stands under the Errors section ... emits on the caught path, or ends in a bare raise' and 'A caught error that neither emits nor re-raises is a defect.' Site: scripts/review::undriven_reason wraps drive_stack and drive_command in 'except ReviewError as err: return str(err)' and emits no event. The catch stands (it returns a value certification_failures acts on: the failure line), so the standard leaves one compliant form: emit on the caught path through the project's event helper (issues.tasks.event, as main does), then return the reason. Trigger: review certified --sprint <path> on a project with a story whose ## Drive commands section is missing or declares no stack beside a stack line, or whose stack-start line names a placeholder. Path: scripts/review::cmd_certified -> ::certification_failures -> ::undriven_reason -> ::drive_stack raises ReviewError -> caught, no event. Scope: caused by the change (the catch is new; at the base the only ReviewError catch was main's owner frame).

Artifact: story:see-governing-versions, 'I want a way to see which plugin version governs my current session beside the version this project's vendored layer carries, so that version drift is visible.' Code: skills/ok-version/SKILL.md Procedure step 1 now reports the installed ok plugin's version from claude plugin list --json (or installed_plugins.json), and itself says 'The installed version can differ from the version loaded in this session until /reload-plugins or a restart'; step 4 labels it 'Plugin version (installed ok plugin)'. So where the installed and the loaded versions differ, the report names no version that governs the session, which is what the story promises. Work item 9 asked for the installed version (notes item 9 calls, decided by A9 for the label). Scope: caused by the change; the merge decides whether the story or the work item stands, which may be a question for the owner.

Item 19 / B114. Trigger: a project whose repository has no commit yet, with the vendored suite files tracked (git add after a first /ok, no commit), meets a stale rendering on the next /ok (a plugin update or an amend). Path: admin/true-up::materialize_steps -> admin/true-up::uncommitted (no-HEAD branch returns every tracked path: 'if git_lines("rev-parse", "-q", "--verify", "HEAD") is None: return sorted(git_lines("ls-files", ...))') -> each stale tracked file becomes the two DESTRUCTIVE steps -> show=archive_show([path]) -> archive_show: 'changed = uncommitted(paths)' is non-empty, so it returns 'git -C %s diff HEAD -- %s'. Saw: '.ok-planner/bin/docs complete' printed 'DOCS COMPLETE: .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-10-22-guide.md / The completion contract holds. This meets the goal for this documentation sprint.' (exit 0), and the report said '0 held: 0 by run, 0 by ask, 0 by read, 0 by link.' 'docs stamp' then wrote '0 claims in its ledger', and the next window reported the docspec 'current'. Cause: scripts/docs complete_failures (line 531) requires a write task per write/change/drop item and a style task per changed file, but no checker task and no recorded claim for any planned file. The completion contract in skills/plan-docs/doc-sprint-document.md item 1 has the same gap. Under /goal the checker decides from this command's output alone, so a run that skips the fact loop meets the goal with unchecked claims, and the empty ledger means the next run never checks those claims either.

In a scratch project with docspec 'guide' stamped by a documentation sprint over docs/guide.md, I deleted .ok-planner/docspec/guide.md, as a sprint's '### Retire docspec: guide' delta does, regenerated the index, and committed. The sprint build prompt (skills/_sprint/shared.md) tells builders to 'Leave every file under the ## Where of a docspec ... as it stands', so the retiring sprint does not remove the files either. Nothing in the suite ever drops or checks them again. The same applies when an Amend docspec delta moves '## Where': the DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT in core.md reads only 'files under the docspec's ## Where as they stand' (step 1, 'Per file under the Where'), and a 'drop' is only 'a file the layout no longer calls for' under that Where, so the files at the old path are left behind. The story promises: after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands. In both cases stale documentation stays in the tree, outside every window, describing a product that has moved on.

The story promises: the policies a codebase follows are recorded as citable artifacts naming the population and condition, so an agent can tell which policy accounts for a construct; plan-sprint SKILL.md line 142 sends gaps and collisions to the intake to be walked like any other issue, and artifact-definitions.md says ' takes , , , , , and  slugs'. The script only knows FOLDERS = {"concept": "concepts", "story": "stories", "decision": "decisions"}, skips any artifact whose kind is not in FOLDERS ('if kind not in FOLDERS: continue'), gathers only .ok-planner/design/, and returns early with no output when design/ holds nothing ('if not docs: return 0'). SKILL.md line 153 then tells the walker: 'Where the script prints nothing, the issue is either about pure code with no corpus commitment or about a concept the record failed to name: flag it to the owner.' body: In a scratch repo (repo/app is the project root holding .ok-planner/, trued up with the working tree's true-up core; repo/lib is a sibling folder of owned code), declared {"folders": ["../lib"]} in app/.ok-planner/config.json (config-check exit 0), committed app/tests/a_test.js and lib/tests/b_test.js, then ran 'python3 .ok-planner/bin/tests window --json' from repo/app. The story promises: a way to declare every folder the project owns so that no check the suite runs over the project misses code it owns. Saw: the window's 'unmapped' list (the test files no scenario claims, which /plan-tests SKILL.md step 2 turns into sort tasks: adopt, port, or delete) names only the in-root test; the test in the declared folder is missing, so /plan-tests never sorts, adopts, or runs it. Every other check honors the declaration: the lint ('plumbline .', no-arg 'plumbline', the post-edit hook) reports comment-hygiene, citation-unresolved, and no-tests violations under ../lib only once folders is declared; 'review files', 'review changed', 'review checks', 'review areas', 'review snapshot', and 'discover areas' all list ../lib/util/b.js. Evidence: tests window --json printed: {"stamp": null, "scenarios": 0, "tests": 0, ..., "unmapped": ["tests/a_test.js"], "edited_tests": [], "changed": 0, "status": "new"} (exit 0), while the lint over the same tree printed '.../repo/lib/tests/b_test.js:1: plumbline/no-tests: a test file is added or edited only inside a test sprint (path matches tests/)', showing the suite does treat ../lib/tests/b_test.js as a test file of the project.

Reviewed /plan-sprint's Sign-off step and the compliance reviewer prompt it dispatches. SKILL.md step 7 (line 175) says: 'Walk with the owner only a judgment finding that meets {{OWNER-QUESTION-TEST}}; settle every other one as a call the rules decide, and list it at Approval. Re-dispatch until clean.' The reviewer prompt in skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md has only a [REVIEW SCOPE] slot. It has no slot for findings the owner already settled (the implementation notes review has one, [SETTLED], core.md line 415). So when the owner answers a judgment finding by keeping the flagged text (for example, the existence-test question 'the owner retires the concept or names the neighbor it merges into', where the owner keeps the concept), or when the session settles a finding as a call that keeps the text, the next dispatch flags it again. 'Until clean' then ends only once the session rewrites the text against the owner's answer, or never ends. The story promises: a signed-off sprint reached 'without ... deciding my open questions for me'. Saw: the text gives the session no path to a clean review that keeps an owner's answer, short of overriding that answer. Evidence: SKILL.md:175 'Re-dispatch until clean.'; design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md:35 'Replace [REVIEW SCOPE]; everything else is invariant.'; core.md:415 'Settled by the owner, and not raised again: [SETTLED].' (notes review only).

In a scratch project trued up from the working tree, wrote a sprint from the template in sprint-document.md with no approval mark and ran the command its goal rule names: '.ok-planner/bin/review certified --sprint .ok-planner/sprints/2026-10-22-plan-a-sprint-526f99f3-draft.md'. Exit 2. Output: 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE: ...-draft.md' / '- ... carries no approval mark, so it may be a draft the owner never approved; if you approved it, add approved: <date> ...' / 'The completion contract does not hold yet. Keep working toward the goal for this sprint file.' The approval refusal goes through the same verdict as an unfinished sprint (scripts/review:1741-1743 calls certified_verdict(sprint, [refusal]); certified_verdict prints the 'Keep working toward the goal' line at scripts/review:1763). Under /goal, the checker reads only that output, so it tells the session to keep working on a draft the owner never approved, while the sprint's step 2 tells the session to stop. The story promises: a signed-off sprint any executor can act on; decision:sprints-carry-an-approval-mark says 'Every executor of a sprint refuses to execute one that carries no mark ... the command that checks the completion contract' and exists because 'an executor pointed at it would build work the owner never approved'. Saw: the command's last line asks the session to continue on the unapproved draft instead of refusing it.

Reviewed /plan-sprint's Terminal step and the sprint's execution boilerplate it writes. SKILL.md Terminal step 3 (line 220) moves the discovery the sprint took up to .ok-planner/history/discoveries/ ('git mv for a tracked file'), and line 227 lists 'the sketches and the discovery it moves' among the files the session writes. The sprint's step 2 (sprint-document.md:100-103) lists the files the planning session leaves uncommitted as 'this file, its delta sidecar, .ok-planner/release-boundaries.md, the intake's two files ..., and the sketches it archived': the discovery is missing. The archive-and-commit step 3 (sprint-document.md:272-278) stages 'every path the sprint's change touched, every moved file at its new path, the /converge run's ledger and folder, and the intake's two files' and commits 'those paths alone with git commit -- <paths>', so the discovery's move (and the archived sketches) stays staged and uncommitted after the close. The story promises: a self-sufficient sprint any executor carries to its close; decision:corpus-audit-hands-a-discovery-to-planning says one discovery stands until a planning session takes it up. Saw: the close commit leaves the take-up of the discovery out of history, so any other clone still holds the discovery under .ok-planner/discoveries/ as standing. Evidence: sprint-document.md:103 '.ok-planner/history/issues.jsonl), and the sketches it archived.'; sprint-document.md:276 'Commit those paths alone with git commit -- <paths>'.

Reviewed the converge skill's close against the story and decision converge-close-takes-vetoes, then ran its tracker steps in a scratch project (trued up from the working tree): opened the run's ledger with tasks init converge-..., recorded a decline and a not-owed failure, ran tasks calls (it printed both rows), then ran the tasks init triage-issues-... that the nested /triage-issues run makes (triage-issues/SKILL.md:40), and ran tasks calls again. The story promises: the owner meets only the questions that need judgment, and the decision promises that every close presents the table of calls the agents made without the owner and asks which rows the owner vetoes. Saw: converge SKILL.md:127 says 'Where the owner list wrote or turned any issue, run /triage-issues next, before the return.' The nested triage's 'tasks init' rewrites the tracker pointer (.ok-planner/.cache/current) to the triage ledger, and nothing in converge's SKILL.md selects the converge ledger again (its only mention of 'tasks use' is 'Never tasks use an existing file.' at :54). The return then reads the wrong ledger: SKILL.md:152 'calls ... what tasks calls prints', :155 'cost: the usage tasks status totals', and :151's 'review drives --confirm --dry-run'. With the triage ledger selected, tasks calls prints 'None.', and SKILL.md:157 says 'Where tasks calls printed None., ask nothing beyond the offer.' So whenever the owner list writes any issue, the run's declines, duplicates, not-owed sorts, and rejections never reach the owner for veto, and the return's cost and unconfirmed-defect lines describe the triage run. Evidence (scratch project): before: 'run: converge-2026-10-22T101500 ... | i5 | declined | session | src/calc.py:add | stands: no harm | / | i6 | not-owed | ...'; after 'tasks init triage-issues-2026-10-22T101700': 'run: triage-issues-2026-10-22T101700 (.ok-planner/tasks/triage-issues-2026-10-22T101700.jsonl)' and tasks calls printed 'None.'; tasks item list --pool defects --key gate --json printed '[]'.

Reviewed the merge prompt's drive-failure rules against the confirm step the converge skill runs (SKILL.md Loop 2 step 6), then in a scratch project added a verified drive defect (source=drive) whose story field named two stories, as merge.md:46 directs, and ran review drives --confirm --dry-run and review drives --confirm. The story promises defects found and fixed without the owner; the skill's confirm step is how a drive defect's fix is checked against its story. Saw: merge.md:46 says 'Two failures with one cause are one defect naming both stories.' while the same paragraph gives only '--field story=<slug>' and, unlike variants ('joined by , '), no form for two stories. scripts/review assumes one slug per defect: confirm_briefs (review:1276-1283) uses fields['story'] whole as the story, and drive_names (review:1250-1263) builds '<story>-<digest>' and raises when it does not match [a-z0-9-]+. A defect written 'story=a, b' makes review drives --confirm refuse the whole call, so no confirm driver is filed for any pending defect of the run, the end check's final confirm (SKILL.md Loop 2 step 2) fails the same way, and every verified drive defect ends the run unconfirmed. The refusal also tells the session to 'rename its story', which is not the cause. A defect that names only one slug instead confirms on one story and never re-drives the other. Evidence: dry run printed '{"pending": [{"defect": "i8", "story": "ffd-demo, ffd-other"}]}'; review drives --confirm printed 'review: the drive name '\''ffd-demo, ffd-other-90607135'\'' holds a character outside [a-z0-9-]+; rename its story' with exit 1.

Trued up a fresh scratch project from the working tree's true-up core (it creates no .ok-planner/design/), and ran the drive mode's first step, review stories, as converge SKILL.md:78 directs ('review stories lists every story by slug'). The story promises defects across the product found and fixed without the owner. Saw: with no .ok-planner/design/stories/ folder, review stories (story_slugs, scripts/review:1449-1454) refuses instead of listing nothing, and review drives refuses the same way. The skill's text expects an empty list: sprint mode step 4 (SKILL.md:104) says 'Where review stories prints no slug, skip the drive and say so in the return', and drive mode gives no branch for a refusal at step 1, so a session that follows the text meets an error mid-Loop 1 with no instruction to go on to Loop 2, where the backlog's defects it already merged would be fixed. review certified, by contrast, reads a missing folder as 'the project has no story' (certification_failures, review:1674), so the verbs disagree on the same state. Evidence: 'review: cannot list .ok-planner/design/stories: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: ...run-6f24ecd9c213/project/.ok-planner/design/stories' with exit 1; 'ls .ok-planner/design' after true-up printed 'No such file or directory'.

body: Reviewed /converge drive step 2 against the drive commands true-up writes for a project whose stack key declares start, then ran those exact commands in a scratch project (trued up with plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up --go-ahead, which wrote them). In order: (1) review drive-command --role stack-start printed '.ok-planner/bin/stack up --name drive'; run 1 ran it, exit 0, tag run-a08eebd11fd5, WEB_PORT=43568, and curl http://127.0.0.1:43568/whoami.txt answered run-a08eebd11fd5. (2) A second verification run ran the same stack-start; stack refused: 'stack: the run run-a08eebd11fd5 holds the name drive, and pid(s) 32988, 32991 still run in its process group; stack down --name drive takes it down'. (3) The second run then did what SKILL.md step 2 says after a failed start ('Where the start fails, the drive ends: ... file and drain step 4's stack-stop task, which takes down what the failed start left'): it ran stack-stop '.ok-planner/bin/stack down --name drive; s=$?; .ok-planner/bin/stack cleanup; exit $s', which printed 'took down: run-a08eebd11fd5 (API_PORT=43569, WEB_PORT=43568; ...)', exit 0. (4) Run 1's server is gone: curl to 43568 exit 7, and stack list no longer holds run-a08eebd11fd5. The failed second run tore down the first run's live stack. Divergent texts: SKILL.md step 2 (quoted above); ADMINISTRATION.md 'Stack declaration' and 'review-facts' fix every drive to the one name drive; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md says 'after a failed start no run holds the name, and down --name exits 0', false when the start failed because another run holds the name. Context: two /converge sessions in one checkout also share the tracker pointer at .ok-planner/.cache/current, so this needs a second verification run that uses the drive's commands. The story promises: 'a way to run isolated verification stacks side by side, so that one verification run never disturbs another's results'; run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run has down remove what a run made. Saw: a refused start's teardown removes another run's stack while that run still verifies. Evidence: the quoted outputs above.

In a scratch project trued up from the working tree, with ports [WEB_PORT, API_PORT] and the range /ok suggested (43550-43749, written through true-up amend), three concurrent bare 'stack up' calls each got their own tag and ports (43554/5, 43550/1, 43552/3), and each server answered with its own tag. down of one left the others serving. A run whose server crashed read connection refused, and the next up got fresh ports (43556/7), not the crashed run's. A foreign program holding a leased port made up retry with a fresh tag (STACK.START.RETRIED attempt 2) and succeed. Two docker-backed runs: down of one swept its network and volume and left the other's. All of that achieved the benefit. Then docker's daemon hung for a few minutes on this machine (docker ps -q still hanging after 8s; another driver's 'docker ps -a -q --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=run-be8ad7b2f2c4' hung too). During that window '.ok-planner/bin/stack up --name drive' sat for over 2.5 minutes with the run entry recorded as 'no ports' and no run folder, its child '/usr/local/bin/docker ps -a -q' hung, until I killed it (exit 143). A separate '.ok-planner/bin/ports lease run-b27174a2f8e5' for a fresh tag also never returned, killed by a 20 s alarm (rc 142). The story promises: verification stacks side by side; ports --help says 'Where docker's daemon does not answer, lease skips the docker check', and ports-leased-from-a-project-range treats a docker-published port as taken only as a narrowing. Saw: a daemon that hangs, rather than refusing, stops every new run's lease with no bound and no message, so one stuck local tool stalls every verification run of the project. Once docker answered again, a lease returned at once (WEB_PORT=43570). Evidence: ps showed 'PID 30613 ... .ok-planner/bin/stack up --name drive' (elapsed 02:25) with child '30620 /usr/local/bin/docker ps -a -q' (elapsed 02:36); 'lease rc=142'.

body: Reviewed /plan-docs (SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) and the docs script it calls, then ran plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs in a scratch project under the scratchpad (not the shared stack: stack up hung on 'docker version', see below). Scratch steps: surface intent with class 'The CLI verbs' declared in src/cli.py; reference docspec listing it; stamped; added verbs sync, push, pull to src/cli.py without touching docs/reference/verbs.md; docs window reported 'reached' ('declaring file changed: src/cli.py'). Wrote a documentation sprint whose docspec heading carries only 'No item: nothing its reader sees changed.' (the planner's verdict SKILL.md:43 allows), opened its run, wrote the report: 'docs complete' printed 'DOCS COMPLETE' (exit 0); after archive and commit, 'docs stamp' printed 'stamped: docspec:reference at c9f1bea..., 0 claims in its ledger', and 'docs window' then printed 'status: current' while 'grep -c pull docs/reference/verbs.md' printed 0. Diverging text: SKILL.md:43 'A docspec in the window whose planner returned no item has nothing behind: keep its heading with the one line No item..., so the run's stamp moves it forward'; doc-sprint-document.md step 7 files checker tasks only over files, and only 'The first checker task of a docspec in round 1 also lists the classes its ## Lists names' (line 111-113), so a no-item docspec gets no checker and no second listing; the completion contract (line 162-166) and docs complete check that every docspec with a ## Generator has its run recorded, but nothing checks that a listed docspec's class listing ran. The story promises: 'name every element I made public and no element I kept internal, so that a reader can depend on what the reference lists'; decision surface-members-listed-at-need: 'A documentation sprint's writer lists the members of each class its docspec names as it writes, and its checker lists them again to check that the documentation misses none.' Saw: one planner agent's no-item verdict on a reached reference docspec moves its stamp past the missing public members with no checker listing, and the next window reports it current, so the missing verbs never reach the reference. Evidence: 'DOCS COMPLETE: .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-10-22-reference-no-item.md'; 'docspec:reference stamp: c9f1bea127915f9e977da725ace510002e554c28 status: current'.

Ran plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs window in a scratch project under the scratchpad. Surface intent classes: 'CLI verbs' and 'Published env vars: every TOOL_* environment variable tool reads is public'; '## Where each class is declared' holds only '- CLI verbs: src/cli.py'. Reference docspec '## Lists': '- CLI verbs', '- Published env vars'. Stamped, then committed src/config.py adding TOOL_TOKEN (docs/reference/env.md lists only TOOL_HOME): 'docs window' printed 'docspec:reference stamp: 634c1e6... status: current' with no reason and no note. Second case: Lists bullet and class rule read 'The CLI verbs' while the declaring line read '- CLI verbs: src/cli.py' (one word apart, the same class to a reader); after adding verb push to src/cli.py, 'docs window' printed 'status: current'. With the declaring line renamed to match, the same change printed 'declaring file changed: src/cli.py' and 'reached'. Diverging code: docs declaring_paths (line 209) keeps only declaring lines whose normalized class name equals a Lists bullet exactly, and window_entry (line 315-321) silently skips a listed class that matches no declaring line; the compliance reviewer's 'Declaring lines' check (skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md:286) requires each line to name a class the rules name, but nothing requires every public class to have one, and plan-docs core.md planner step 7 names 'a listed class the surface intent does not name' as a reshape gap but not a listed class with no declaring line. The story promises: 'name every element I made public ... so that a reader can depend on what the reference lists'; decision surface-members-listed-at-need: 'the surface intent names the files that declare the class's members' and 'Whoever needs a class's members lists them from the tree at that moment, starting from the files the surface intent names as declaring the class'. Saw: a new public member of a listed class whose declaring line is missing or worded differently never opens the window, the run is never planned, and the reference silently omits it. Evidence: 'docspec:reference stamp: 634c1e689074b86410f647673f47f1921c2ec6a2 status: current' after 'ENV = ["TOOL_HOME", "TOOL_TOKEN"]'.

Read the {{DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT}} in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/core.md. Its plan numbers the worked-example draft as step 6 (line 131-134) and the reshape gaps, among them 'a listed class the surface intent does not name', as step 7 (line 135-138), but its Output says (line 153): 'Then Reshape: and one line per gap step 6 found, or none.' A planner that follows the Output literally reports the example-draft step under Reshape and can drop the step-7 gaps, so a ## Lists bullet that names no class of the surface intent, whose members the run then cannot list, does not reach the owner as work for /plan-sprint (SKILL.md step 4: 'Name each reshape a planner returned to the owner'). The story promises: 'name every element I made public and no element I kept internal'; decision every-public-class-has-a-reference: each public class 'is named in the lists of at least one reference docspec'. Saw: the reshape report points at the wrong step. Evidence: core.md:153 'one line per gap step 6 found'; core.md:135 '7. Name what keeps the docspec from being planned well: ... a listed class the surface intent does not name'.

Reviewed /converge drive mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md steps 2 and 4) with the stack lines true-up writes (admin/ADMINISTRATION.md 'Stack declaration': stack-start '.ok-planner/bin/stack up --name drive', stack-stop '.ok-planner/bin/stack down --name drive; s=$?; .ok-planner/bin/stack cleanup; exit $s'), then ran those exact lines in a trued-up scratch project with a compose stack built under RUN_TAG. SKILL.md step 2 says 'Where the start fails, the drive ends: ... file and drain step 4's stack-stop task, which takes down what the failed start left'; docs/stack-helpers.md line 443 says 'after a failed start no run holds the name, and down --name exits 0'. That is false when the start failed because another live verification run in the same checkout holds the fixed name drive: the second run's stop line then takes down the first run's live stack and releases its leased ports, which the registry can lease to a later run while the first run's drivers still address them. The story promises: each verification run builds and resolves its own artifacts, so no run can pick up another run's (concept run-tag: 'Concurrent runs cannot collide on an artifact or on a stack'). Saw: first run 'stack up --name drive' -> 'run-cfc94a3e1f1b / WEB_PORT=44856', exit 0; second run's start -> 'stack: the run run-cfc94a3e1f1b holds the name drive, and 1 running container(s) carry its label or belong to its compose project; stack down --name drive takes it down', exit 1; second run's stop line -> 'took down: run-cfc94a3e1f1b (WEB_PORT=44856; 1 container(s), 1 network(s), 0 volume(s), 1 image(s))', exit 0; first run's verify by its own tag -> 'no artifact carries tag run-cfc94a3e1f1b', exit 1. The stop line keys on the shared name, not on the tag the run's own start minted, so one run's teardown reaches another run's stack.

The story promises: 'a way to see which plugin version governs my current session beside the version this project's vendored layer carries, so that version drift is visible.' Saw: step 1 now reports the installed version, not the governing one, and the skill says so itself: '### 1. Installed plugin version' ... 'The installed version can differ from the version loaded in this session until /reload-plugins or a restart'; the report line reads '**Plugin version (installed ok plugin):**', where the committed text read '**Plugin version (governing this session):**'. After a 'claude plugin update' and before a reload or restart, a session that follows this text reports a plugin version that does not govern the session, under a label that tells the owner it is the installed one. So the skill gives no value for the version governing the current session, which is what the story's capability names. The conduct line still reports the governing version ('Conduct version (governing this session)'), so the three lines mix an installed value with governing values. Either the skill reports the version loaded in the session, or the story's capability changes to name the installed version (a corpus change for /plan-sprint). The drift the 'so that' clause names, plugin against vendored stamp, is visible with the new step 1 when the installed version and the loaded version agree.

body: Reviewed /plan-tests (SKILL.md step 5.2, core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT, TEST-LEGACY-PROMPT, TEST-SWEEP-PROMPT, TEST-FIX-PROMPT) and scripts/tests (assembled_plan, plan_failures, stage_write, live_tests, stray_paths). The sort decides fixtures before it can know which tests are adopted, and no later step corrects that decision. SKILL.md step 5.2 files 'one sort task per ten of them, in path order', and the drain runs those tasks side by side. A fixture under tests/fixtures/ usually sits in a different batch from the tests that read it. The sort table says: 'It is a fixture or a helper that an adopted test uses. | support, naming the scenarios it serves'. An agent sorting the fixture's batch cannot see the adopt decisions another batch has not yet made. Nothing after the sort reconciles fixtures with adopted tests: tests plan checks only that a support entry names planned scenarios ('support names a scenario the plan lacks'), the plan review checks only ports and adopts, and the sweep acts only on files no record claims. (1) A fixture an adopted test reads that gets sorted 'delete' is removed by its legacy task. The adopted test then fails, and TEST-FIX-PROMPT forbids the fix: 'you change no test: no file at a test path, no support file, no fixture'. The fix tasks close blocked twice and the run stops at a genuine blocker. The test that guarded a promise is lost. (2) A fixture sorted 'support' whose adopted test does not use it is claimed through legacy_support in live_tests, so stray_paths never lists it and the sweep never deletes it. Part of the old suite stays. The story promises: keep the tests that check what my product promises and drop the rest. decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'So is a fixture or a data file no kept test uses [deleted]'. Saw: no step bases the support or delete sort of a fixture on the final set of adopted tests. evidence: SKILL.md step 5.2 'file one sort task per ten of them, in path order'; core.md sort table row 'It is a fixture or a helper that an adopted test uses'; scripts/tests live_tests 'legacy_support = {e["path"] for e in plan["legacy"] if e["sort"] == "support" and s["id"] in e["scenarios"]}'.

Reviewed /plan-tests SKILL.md step 2 (the runner), core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT, and scripts/tests plan_failures and assembled_plan. When testing.run holds no {name}, the sort works one file at a time, and the decision promises a sort of each test. core.md: 'Sort each test: each test by its name where testing.run in .ok-planner/config.json holds {name}, each file otherwise.' SKILL.md step 2 includes {name} only 'where the runner needs a test's name inside its file', and the owner may accept a file-level runner such as 'npx jest {path}'. Under a file-level runner: (1) a legacy file that holds one promise test and several orphan tests is adopted whole, so its orphans stay, along with the imports of private code that block a removal; (2) a file whose tests check two scenarios can be adopted into only one of them, because scripts/tests plan_failures refuses 'scenarios %s and %s share the test %s' and locator() is the bare path. The second scenario then gets a new test, and its legacy tests stay inside the adopted file as duplicates the plan never deletes. The story promises: drop the rest, so that the old suite does not block my changes. decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'sorts every test no scenario claims ... A test that checks the code against itself, or a behavior no story or rule names, is an orphan, and is deleted' and 'Where two legacy tests check one scenario, the first is adopted and the second deleted'. Saw: with a file-level runner the skill sorts files, not tests, and no step asks for a runner that addresses one test when a legacy suite is present. evidence: core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT 'each file otherwise'; scripts/tests locator() 'return "%s::%s" % (test["path"], test["name"]) if test.get("name") else test["path"]'.

Reviewed test-sprint-document.md 'How to execute this test sprint' step 8 and the archive step, and scripts/tests cmd_report and cmd_complete. The decision promises the owner a veto over each deletion and each port, but the boilerplate defines what to do only for a vetoed call. Step 8: 'Present the completion report to the owner: each test written, rewritten, retired, or recorded as a gap, the legacy tests ported and deleted, ... and each call an agent made, for the owner's veto. For each vetoed call, file one issue ...'. Deletions and ports are plan legacy entries and ports-pool items, not calls. For a vetoed deletion or port, no step restores the test, no step files an issue, and nothing keeps the deletion out of the archive commit, which stages 'every path the run's tasks staged'. By this point tests complete has written the -complete.txt mark, so the lint's no-tests check refuses any agent's edit that would restore a test outside a test sprint. The story promises: keep the tests that check what my product promises. decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'The completion report lists each deletion and each port for the owner's veto, and git history keeps every deleted test.' Saw: a vetoed deletion or port has no defined effect. evidence: test-sprint-document.md step 8 'For each vetoed call, file one issue'; scripts/tests cmd_report lists 'Legacy tests deleted' and 'Legacy tests ported' apart from 'Calls'.

(exit 0). No ledger was created for them: .ok-planner/.cache/read/ held only owner-sna-36378981.json, patrick-meehan-79ab22ae.json, peer-sna-b1cfeb63.json. Triage then answered that very question: 'issues respond see-new-analysis-first-run' with replies_to [1] -> 'responded see-new-analysis-first-run: replies=1 changed=- seen=1'. The third person's first 'issues list --unread' then created their ledger counting everything as read and printed nothing (exit 0); 'list --json' gave 'see-new-analysis-first-run unread= 0 unopened= False', and 'show' printed the reply with no 'new' mark ('2. triage reply to 1 2026-10-22T10:23:20Z'). The owner, whose ledger already existed, saw the same issue as 'unread=2 never read'. The same thing happened on the dashboard project: peer-sna-dash commented on two issues before ever listing, and their first 'issues list --unread' after a triage reply, a triage update, and the owner's comment printed nothing. Cause: the ledger is created by the first read-type call ('a reader with a name creates that name s ledger the first time'), not by the person's first write. So a person who starts by commenting loses every answer and revision that lands before they first list. The story promises: 'see which open issues arrived since I began working the intake ... or have new answers or revisions since I last read them, whoever wrote them'. decision:read-marks-kept-per-person says 'A fresh ledger, in a new clone or on a person's first run, starts with everything that exists counted as read'; a comment is a person's first run of working the intake. Saw: the triage reply to the person's own question never counts as new to them. Evidence: quoted above; scratch helper scripts s6.sh / d4.sh.

(exit 0); 'tasks --file <converge ledger> calls' still printed the three rows. SKILL.md 'What the run leaves for the owner' says: 'Where the owner list wrote or turned any issue, run /triage-issues next, before the return.' /triage-issues opens 'a fresh ledger' with 'tasks init', which moves the tracker pointer (.ok-planner/.cache/current) to the triage ledger. The return then says: 'calls ... what `tasks calls` prints' and 'Where `tasks calls` printed `None.`, ask nothing beyond the offer.' No --file names the converge ledger (the sprint boilerplate step 13 does pass --file for exactly this reason: 'because /converge moved the tracker's pointer to its own ledger'). So whenever the owner list writes any issue, the return shows the triage ledger's calls (None.) and asks no veto; the same applies to 'cost' (tasks status, tasks report). the story promises: the owner sees every call made in their absence so they can overturn one; decision converge-close-takes-vetoes: 'Its close presents the table of the calls its agents made without the owner ... and asks which rows the owner vetoes.' saw: the run's calls are dropped from the close whenever triage ran. evidence: 'after triage init: .ok-planner/tasks/triage-issues-veto.jsonl' / 'None.' vs '| i1 | declined | session | c.py::h | ...' under --file.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:The return (drive, analysis, defects mode). What the code does: SKILL.md:127 runs /triage-issues before the return wherever the owner list wrote or turned an issue; /triage-issues step 2 (triage-issues/SKILL.md:40) opens its own ledger with 'tasks init', which moves the tracker pointer (.ok-planner/.cache/current) off the converge ledger, and nothing in converge's SKILL.md selects the converge ledger again or passes --file. The return then reads the triage ledger: SKILL.md:152 'calls ... what `tasks calls` prints', SKILL.md:155 'cost: the usage `tasks status` totals and the task count from `tasks report`', and SKILL.md:151's 'review drives --confirm --dry-run'. Trigger: any drive, analysis, or defects run whose owner list writes or turns an issue. Harm (A9): the return tells the owner the run made no calls ('None.') when its agents declined, sorted not-owed, or rejected items, and SKILL.md:157 'Where `tasks calls` printed `None.`, ask nothing beyond the offer' then asks no veto, so the owner acts on a false report and cannot overturn a call made in their absence (story veto-calls-made-in-my-absence; decision converge-close-takes-vetoes 'Its close presents the table of the calls its agents made without the owner ... and asks which rows the owner vetoes'); the cost and unconfirmed-defect lines describe the triage run. In scope: sprint work item 18 (B18) rewrote this return to take vetoes from 'tasks calls', so the change makes its promised outcome fail through this site. Evidence: driver scratch run, after 'tasks init triage-issues-veto --file .ok-planner/tasks/triage-issues-veto.jsonl' 'tasks calls' printed 'None.' while 'tasks --file <converge ledger> calls' printed the three rows; the sprint close (plan-sprint/sprint-document.md step 13) passes --file for this reason. Failures: i45 (veto-calls-made-in-my-absence); the same flaw is failure i31 (find-and-fix-defects, merged by t41).

Reviewed /converge's close in drive/analysis/defects mode, then ran the tracker it calls in a scratch project (stack run, trued up): init a converge ledger with the skill's calls config, added a declined defect, a not-owed failure, and an unlisted call; 'tasks calls' printed the three rows; then 'tasks init triage-issues-veto --file .ok-planner/tasks/triage-issues-veto.jsonl' (what /triage-issues step 2 runs), after which 'tasks calls' printed 'None.' (exit 0); 'tasks --file <converge ledger> calls' still printed the three rows. SKILL.md 'What the run leaves for the owner' says: 'Where the owner list wrote or turned any issue, run /triage-issues next, before the return.' /triage-issues opens 'a fresh ledger' with 'tasks init', which moves the tracker pointer (.ok-planner/.cache/current) to the triage ledger. The return then says: 'calls ... what `tasks calls` prints' and 'Where `tasks calls` printed `None.`, ask nothing beyond the offer.' No --file names the converge ledger (the sprint boilerplate step 13 does pass --file for exactly this reason: 'because /converge moved the tracker's pointer to its own ledger'). So whenever the owner list writes any issue, the return shows the triage ledger's calls (None.) and asks no veto; the same applies to 'cost' (tasks status, tasks report). the story promises: the owner sees every call made in their absence so they can overturn one; decision converge-close-takes-vetoes: 'Its close presents the table of the calls its agents made without the owner ... and asks which rows the owner vetoes.' saw: the run's calls are dropped from the close whenever triage ran. evidence: 'after triage init: .ok-planner/tasks/triage-issues-veto.jsonl' / 'None.' vs '| i1 | declined | session | c.py::h | ...' under --file.

Reviewed /plan-tests SKILL.md step 2 (the runner), core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT, and scripts/tests plan_failures and assembled_plan. When testing.run holds no {name}, the sort works one file at a time, and the decision promises a sort of each test. core.md: 'Sort each test: each test by its name where testing.run in .ok-planner/config.json holds {name}, each file otherwise.' SKILL.md step 2 includes {name} only 'where the runner needs a test's name inside its file', and the owner may accept a file-level runner such as 'npx jest {path}'. Under a file-level runner: (1) a legacy file that holds one promise test and several orphan tests is adopted whole, so its orphans stay, along with the imports of private code that block a removal; (2) a file whose tests check two scenarios can be adopted into only one of them, because scripts/tests plan_failures refuses 'scenarios %s and %s share the test %s' and locator() is the bare path. The second scenario then gets a new test, and its legacy tests stay inside the adopted file as duplicates the plan never deletes. The story promises: drop the rest, so that the old suite does not block my changes. decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'sorts every test no scenario claims ... A test that checks the code against itself, or a behavior no story or rule names, is an orphan, and is deleted' and 'Where two legacy tests check one scenario, the first is adopted and the second deleted'. Saw: with a file-level runner the skill sorts files, not tests, and no step asks for a runner that addresses one test when a legacy suite is present. evidence: core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT 'each file otherwise'; scripts/tests locator() 'return "%s::%s" % (test["path"], test["name"]) if test.get("name") else test["path"]'.

Entry: A8, decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically Choice 'sorts every test no scenario claims' and 'A test that checks the code against itself, or a behavior no story or rule names, is an orphan, and is deleted'; under a file-level runner a legacy file holding a promise test and orphan tests is adopted whole, so its orphans stay, and a file whose tests check two scenarios is adopted into one, its other tests kept as duplicates the plan never deletes (story retire-a-legacy-suite: 'drop the rest'). body: Reviewed test-sprint-document.md 'How to execute this test sprint' step 8 and the archive step, and scripts/tests cmd_report and cmd_complete. The decision promises the owner a veto over each deletion and each port, but the boilerplate defines what to do only for a vetoed call. Step 8: 'Present the completion report to the owner: each test written, rewritten, retired, or recorded as a gap, the legacy tests ported and deleted, ... and each call an agent made, for the owner's veto. For each vetoed call, file one issue ...'. Deletions and ports are plan legacy entries and ports-pool items, not calls. For a vetoed deletion or port, no step restores the test, no step files an issue, and nothing keeps the deletion out of the archive commit, which stages 'every path the run's tasks staged'. By this point tests complete has written the -complete.txt mark, so the lint's no-tests check refuses any agent's edit that would restore a test outside a test sprint. The story promises: keep the tests that check what my product promises. decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'The completion report lists each deletion and each port for the owner's veto, and git history keeps every deleted test.' Saw: a vetoed deletion or port has no defined effect. evidence: test-sprint-document.md step 8 'For each vetoed call, file one issue'; scripts/tests cmd_report lists 'Legacy tests deleted' and 'Legacy tests ported' apart from 'Calls'.

body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (run-08eb6254adec), a third person set a name (XDG_CONFIG_HOME=config-c issues name --set third-sna) and made a comment their first act on the intake: 'issues comment see-new-analysis-first-run --text "third-sna: which option is cheaper?"' (exit 0). No ledger was created for them: .ok-planner/.cache/read/ held only owner-sna-36378981.json, patrick-meehan-79ab22ae.json, peer-sna-b1cfeb63.json. Triage then answered that very question: 'issues respond see-new-analysis-first-run' with replies_to [1] -> 'responded see-new-analysis-first-run: replies=1 changed=- seen=1'. The third person's first 'issues list --unread' then created their ledger counting everything as read and printed nothing (exit 0); 'list --json' gave 'see-new-analysis-first-run unread= 0 unopened= False', and 'show' printed the reply with no 'new' mark ('2. triage reply to 1 2026-10-22T10:23:20Z'). The owner, whose ledger already existed, saw the same issue as 'unread=2 never read'. The same thing happened on the dashboard project: peer-sna-dash commented on two issues before ever listing, and their first 'issues list --unread' after a triage reply, a triage update, and the owner's comment printed nothing. Cause: the ledger is created by the first read-type call ('a reader with a name creates that name s ledger the first time'), not by the person's first write. So a person who starts by commenting loses every answer and revision that lands before they first list. The story promises: 'see which open issues arrived since I began working the intake ... or have new answers or revisions since I last read them, whoever wrote them'. decision:read-marks-kept-per-person says 'A fresh ledger, in a new clone or on a person's first run, starts with everything that exists counted as read'; a comment is a person's first run of working the intake. Saw: the triage reply to the person's own question never counts as new to them. Evidence: quoted above; scratch helper scripts s6.sh / d4.sh.
note: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/issues:person_message (comment and rule), with seeded_ledger/held_ledger: a person's write never seeds that person's read ledger, which only a read verb creates (reading_ledger, mark_read), so a fresh ledger made at the first list counts as read every answer and revision that landed after the person's first comment. Entry: A3, the CLI verb 'issues list --unread' gives a wrong result: the driver's third person commented first, triage replied to that question, and the first 'list --unread' printed nothing, 'show' marked the reply not new (story see-new-analysis: 'have new answers or revisions since I last read them ... since I began working the intake'; decision read-marks-kept-per-person: 'A fresh ledger, in a new clone or on a person's first run, starts with everything that exists counted as read'). Outside the sprint: scripts/issues stands the same at base e9949f9 (git diff empty), and no work item of the sprint touches the read ledger.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:backlog_entry. The widened path pattern (review:1027, PATH_ALTERNATIVES = r'[\w.-]*(?:/[\w.-]+)+|[\w./-]+\.\w+') matches absolute extensionless paths such as /usr/bin/env, /bin/sh, or /etc/services. backlog_entry tests os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, token)) (review:1078), and os.path.join with an absolute token returns the token, so a system file passes; left_alone finds no owner path, harness match, or stamp, so the token lands in files (review:1084 files.append(token)). Trigger: an open category: defect issue whose problem names such a path (a shebang, or /etc/services, which project.md itself names). Harm: review backlog reports a file outside the project tree as a file of the tree, as the issue's site and in files, which reach the fix task's --files as a file the run may edit (A9; the A2 write target follows where a fixer acts on it). Scope: caused by the change; the base PATH_PATTERN r'[\w./-]+\.\w+' (base review:1014) required an extension, and B9 widens the match only for files of the tree. From report i15.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:undriven_reason. The new catch 'except ReviewError as err: return str(err)' (review:1698-1699) stands, since certification_failures acts on the reason it returns, but it emits no event and does not re-raise. Rule: .ok-planner/docs/events.md, Where the code emits: 'every error caught: a catch that stands under the Errors section ... emits on the caught path', and 'A caught error that neither emits nor re-raises is a defect.' The one compliant form is an emission through the project's event helper (issues.tasks.event, as main does at review:1930) on the caught path. Trigger: review certified --sprint <path> on a project with a story whose ## Drive commands section is missing, holds a - No stack: line beside a stack line, or whose stack-start line is refused; drive_stack or drive_command raises ReviewError and the catch swallows it with no record. Scope: caused by the change; at the base the only ReviewError catch was main's owner frame. From report i16.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:archive_show. In a repository with no commit, uncommitted() returns every tracked path (true-up:593-594, 'if git_lines("rev-parse", "-q", "--verify", "HEAD") is None: return sorted(git_lines("ls-files", ...))'), so archive_show returns 'git -C <root> diff HEAD -- <path>' (true-up:1389-1391), and git answers 'fatal: bad revision HEAD' with exit 128 there. Trigger: a project with no commit yet whose stamped suite files are tracked (git add after a first /ok), then /ok after a plugin update or an amend that makes those files stale; materialize_steps (true-up:4052-4055) now makes each such file a copy step and a destructive stale step, each with show=archive_show([path]). Harm: /ok step 4 shows the owner the output of each Show: command before the one consent question, and every Show under these steps prints a git error instead of the content the step archives and overwrites, so the owner consents without seeing the work at stake and the error does not say why (A3). ADMINISTRATION.md:44 documents this exact Show for the no-commit case. Scope: archive_show and uncommitted stood at the base, but B114 newly routes stale tracked suite files in a no-HEAD repository through this Show, so the change newly exposes /ok's consent to it. From report i18.

R4/C2 under A2 (and A9). Trigger: an open category: defect issue whose problem names an absolute extensionless path, such as a shebang '#!/usr/bin/env python3', '/bin/sh', or the port registry's '/etc/services' that .ok-planner/review/project.md itself names. Path: scripts/review:cmd_backlog -> scripts/review:backlog_entry -> PATH_PATTERN (PATH_ALTERNATIVES, line 1027: r'[\w.-]*(?:/[\w.-]+)+|[\w./-]+\.\w+'). The new first alternative matches '/usr/bin/env' (an empty prefix, then '/usr', '/bin', '/env'); backlog_entry then tests os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, token)), and os.path.join with an absolute token returns the token itself, so '/usr/bin/env' passes as a file. left_alone('/usr/bin/env') finds no owner path, no harness match, and no suite stamp in the binary's text, so it returns None, and the token lands in files (line 1084: files.append(token)). Harm: the backlog report's files, and through review fixes the fix task's --files, name a system file outside the project tree as a file the run may edit (a write target the run should never reach); an issue that names only such a path and no project file now yields a report with site '/usr/bin/env' instead of going under settled, so the report says the issue names a file of the tree. Scope: caused by the change. The base PATH_PATTERN r'[\w./-]+\.\w+' required an extension, so extensionless absolute paths such as /usr/bin/env, /bin/sh, and /etc/services never matched; absolute paths with an extension stood at the base the same way. B9 lists the widening only for paths inside the tree ('an issue naming only an extensionless file' of the tree).

Build call i15 (t13) left a harm. Trigger: a project whose repository has no commit yet, with the vendored suite files tracked (git add after a first /ok, no commit), meets a stale rendering on the next /ok (a plugin update or an amend). Harm: /ok step 4 shows the owner 'the output of each Show: command under its step' for the one consent; every Show under the copy step and the stale rewrite prints a git error instead of the change the step would archive and overwrite, so the owner consents without seeing the work at stake, and the error does not say why. body: Reviewed /converge drive mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md steps 2 and 4) with the stack lines true-up writes (admin/ADMINISTRATION.md 'Stack declaration': stack-start '.ok-planner/bin/stack up --name drive', stack-stop '.ok-planner/bin/stack down --name drive; s=$?; .ok-planner/bin/stack cleanup; exit $s'), then ran those exact lines in a trued-up scratch project with a compose stack built under RUN_TAG. SKILL.md step 2 says 'Where the start fails, the drive ends: ... file and drain step 4's stack-stop task, which takes down what the failed start left'; docs/stack-helpers.md line 443 says 'after a failed start no run holds the name, and down --name exits 0'. That is false when the start failed because another live verification run in the same checkout holds the fixed name drive: the second run's stop line then takes down the first run's live stack and releases its leased ports, which the registry can lease to a later run while the first run's drivers still address them. The story promises: each verification run builds and resolves its own artifacts, so no run can pick up another run's (concept run-tag: 'Concurrent runs cannot collide on an artifact or on a stack'). Saw: first run 'stack up --name drive' -> 'run-cfc94a3e1f1b / WEB_PORT=44856', exit 0; second run's start -> 'stack: the run run-cfc94a3e1f1b holds the name drive, and 1 running container(s) carry its label or belong to its compose project; stack down --name drive takes it down', exit 1; second run's stop line -> 'took down: run-cfc94a3e1f1b (WEB_PORT=44856; 1 container(s), 1 network(s), 0 volume(s), 1 image(s))', exit 0; first run's verify by its own tag -> 'no artifact carries tag run-cfc94a3e1f1b', exit 1. The stop line keys on the shared name, not on the tag the run's own start minted, so one run's teardown reaches another run's stack.
