body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree, with ports [WEB_PORT, API_PORT] and the range /ok suggested (43550-43749, written through true-up amend), three concurrent bare 'stack up' calls each got their own tag and ports (43554/5, 43550/1, 43552/3), and each server answered with its own tag. down of one left the others serving. A run whose server crashed read connection refused, and the next up got fresh ports (43556/7), not the crashed run's. A foreign program holding a leased port made up retry with a fresh tag (STACK.START.RETRIED attempt 2) and succeed. Two docker-backed runs: down of one swept its network and volume and left the other's. All of that achieved the benefit. Then docker's daemon hung for a few minutes on this machine (docker ps -q still hanging after 8s; another driver's 'docker ps -a -q --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=run-be8ad7b2f2c4' hung too). During that window '.ok-planner/bin/stack up --name drive' sat for over 2.5 minutes with the run entry recorded as 'no ports' and no run folder, its child '/usr/local/bin/docker ps -a -q' hung, until I killed it (exit 143). A separate '.ok-planner/bin/ports lease run-b27174a2f8e5' for a fresh tag also never returned, killed by a 20 s alarm (rc 142). The story promises: verification stacks side by side; ports --help says 'Where docker's daemon does not answer, lease skips the docker check', and ports-leased-from-a-project-range treats a docker-published port as taken only as a narrowing. Saw: a daemon that hangs, rather than refusing, stops every new run's lease with no bound and no message, so one stuck local tool stalls every verification run of the project. Once docker answered again, a lease returned at once (WEB_PORT=43570). Evidence: ps showed 'PID 30613 ... .ok-planner/bin/stack up --name drive' (elapsed 02:25) with child '30620 /usr/local/bin/docker ps -a -q' (elapsed 02:36); 'lease rc=142'.

Outside the sprint: ports and docker-sweep stand the same at base e9949f9, and the sprint's change does not reach them.

body: Reviewed /plan-tests (SKILL.md step 5.2, core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT, TEST-LEGACY-PROMPT, TEST-SWEEP-PROMPT, TEST-FIX-PROMPT) and scripts/tests (assembled_plan, plan_failures, stage_write, live_tests, stray_paths). The sort decides fixtures before it can know which tests are adopted, and no later step corrects that decision. SKILL.md step 5.2 files 'one sort task per ten of them, in path order', and the drain runs those tasks side by side. A fixture under tests/fixtures/ usually sits in a different batch from the tests that read it. The sort table says: 'It is a fixture or a helper that an adopted test uses. | support, naming the scenarios it serves'. An agent sorting the fixture's batch cannot see the adopt decisions another batch has not yet made. Nothing after the sort reconciles fixtures with adopted tests: tests plan checks only that a support entry names planned scenarios ('support names a scenario the plan lacks'), the plan review checks only ports and adopts, and the sweep acts only on files no record claims. (1) A fixture an adopted test reads that gets sorted 'delete' is removed by its legacy task. The adopted test then fails, and TEST-FIX-PROMPT forbids the fix: 'you change no test: no file at a test path, no support file, no fixture'. The fix tasks close blocked twice and the run stops at a genuine blocker. The test that guarded a promise is lost. (2) A fixture sorted 'support' whose adopted test does not use it is claimed through legacy_support in live_tests, so stray_paths never lists it and the sweep never deletes it. Part of the old suite stays. The story promises: keep the tests that check what my product promises and drop the rest. decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'So is a fixture or a data file no kept test uses [deleted]'. Saw: no step bases the support or delete sort of a fixture on the final set of adopted tests. evidence: SKILL.md step 5.2 'file one sort task per ten of them, in path order'; core.md sort table row 'It is a fixture or a helper that an adopted test uses'; scripts/tests live_tests 'legacy_support = {e["path"] for e in plan["legacy"] if e["sort"] == "support" and s["id"] in e["scenarios"]}'.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:inline_body. What the code does: it opens a delta's inline body at the first line matching '^(`{3,})markdown' and ends it at the first later line equal to that same fence (scripts/review:1563-1569), so a final-form body that holds its own ``` code block, fenced with ```markdown, is cut at its first inner fence. Neither the delta form ({{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}}, skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:284) nor the sprint template (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:30-39) says how to fence a body that holds a code block. Trigger: a delta '### New decision: cc-fenced' whose ```markdown body holds '```' / 'make check' / '```', landed byte for byte. Harm (A9): review deltas (cmd_deltas, a path this change added, item 13) lists the landed delta as unsettled ('cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body'), and review certified prints 'item 1 (deltas): fails' and SPRINT NOT COMPLETE over a delta that landed as approved; a C3 fixer that copies the body verbatim cannot clear it. Evidence: driver t5's scratch run, 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE ... - New decision: cc-fenced: .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body' (failures i11, i12).

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/discover:question_failures. What the code does: the assembly refuses any question whose artifact is not a live file (scripts/discover:458-459 'elif read_text(root, live_path(...)) is None: failures.append("%s: artifact %s does not exist" ...)'). This sprint's item 8 removed the other exit: skills/discover-design/SKILL.md step 7 now sends each review finding with decided=no to be 'ask[ed] ... as a question with both answers', and the assembly 'refuses a finding that stands open' (scripts/discover assembled, the new 'it stands open; refile merge task' failure). The review prompt (skills/discover-design/core.md:513-515) makes every promise change the code does not settle a question, and the merge prompt (core.md:370) gives a gap under a proposed slug only a new delta or a drop. Trigger: an empty corpus (every promise change is a new delta), or an out-of-date one where the code holds something no artifact records and prose and code disagree; the merge or the refiled review records the question with artifact=story:read-balance, stale_op=new. Harm (A8): the amended story:bootstrap-design-corpus promises 'the corpus changes it needs plus the questions only I can answer, whether the corpus is empty or out of date', and the new decision:corpus-audit-hands-a-discovery-to-planning 'drafts ... each question only the owner can answer, with both answers'; on a new artifact no question can be asked, so a disagreement the code does not settle is dropped or decided silently as a delta, and an undecided review finding on a new delta can neither stay open nor become a question, so the assembly cannot pass. Evidence: driver t3, 'the discovery does not hold: - question void-counting (item i14, task t16): artifact story:read-balance does not exist', exit 2 (failures i13, i14).

Reviewed the sprint-certification path: /converge sprint, the sprint boilerplate (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md steps 12-13 and the Completion contract), and the scripts it calls (review deltas, review certified). The delta form in skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md {{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}} says: 'Long bodies go in a sidecar, one file per artifact, and the sprint heading reads `body: in the sidecar`'. fix.md and verify.md repeat 'where the heading reads `body: in the sidecar`'. But scripts/review DELTA_HEADING is r'^### (New|Amend|Retire) (?:(concept|story|decision|subject|practice|docspec): (\S+)|surface intent)\s*$', so it only matches a heading that ends at the slug. A heading that carries the pointer, as the form's words say, is not matched, and sprint_deltas() drops that delta without comparing it. Story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint'; decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository: 'One command, `review certified`, checks the contract's items in the repository'; completion contract item 1: 'Every corpus matches every delta above'. Saw: in a scratch project, a sprint with '### New story: cc-sidecar-a — body: in the sidecar' (sidecar file present, artifact never landed), '### New story: cc-sidecar-b' with the line 'body: in the sidecar' under it, and one inline delta. review deltas printed '"compared": 2' and listed nothing for cc-sidecar-a. The certified line 'item 1 (deltas): holds: <n> deltas landed' counts only the parsed deltas. So an approved delta that never landed passes item 1, and the return's deltas line ('<n> compared') undercounts.

Reviewed the sprint-certification path, as in the sibling failure. scripts/review inline_body() opens the delta body at the first line matching '^(`{3,})markdown' and ends it at the first later line equal to that same fence. The delta form ({{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}} in skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md) and the sprint template (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md) say nothing about fencing a body that holds its own code block. So a final-form body that holds a ``` code block, such as a decision that shows a command, is cut short at its first inner fence. Story promises: 'done means the same thing for every sprint'; completion contract item 1: 'Every corpus matches every delta above, applied verbatim'; decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository: certified 'prints SPRINT COMPLETE or SPRINT NOT COMPLETE'. Saw: in a scratch project, the delta '### New decision: cc-fenced' carried a ```markdown body that held '```' / 'make check' / '```'. I copied the whole body into .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md, byte for byte, and regenerated the TOCs. review deltas printed 'unsettled': 'cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body', and review certified printed 'item 1 (deltas): fails' and 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE ... - New decision: cc-fenced: .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body'. A C3 fixer that copies the same body verbatim cannot clear it. A sprint whose delta holds a code block never certifies complete, even though it landed as approved.

In a scratch project (stack up, true-up, git init), I built an approved sprint, a base file, a landed delta, and a converge ledger holding a review task closed done, a drive task, and defects. Then I ran .ok-planner/bin/review approved / certified / deltas through each state. Each of these held: a draft with no mark is refused and named; no completion report fails; an open defect fails; an unlisted stuck defect fails; a listed one passes; a check failing on a changed file fails; a ledger with no drive fails, naming the unfilled drive commands; an archived sprint is found from its sprints/ path; and 'closed:' is terminal. Two parses diverge from the delta form, so 'done' depends on how a delta is written. (1) A heading that carries the sidecar pointer, as {{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}} words it ('the sprint heading reads `body: in the sidecar`'), e.g. '### New story: cc-sidecar-a — body: in the sidecar', is silently skipped. review deltas printed '"compared": 2' for three deltas, and the delta that never landed went unreported. (2) A ```markdown body holding an inner ``` fence is truncated. A verbatim-landed .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md gave 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE ... - New decision: cc-fenced: .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body'. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint'. Saw: certified passes an unlanded delta in case (1) and refuses a landed one in case (2).

Reviewed /discover-design (SKILL.md, core.md, scripts/discover) and ran its steps by hand in a scratch project trued up from the working tree, with an empty corpus (no .ok-planner/design/), a 22-line app/ledger.py, and a README: status, tasks init, prompt register, config set item_states, discover areas, discover surveys, survey items, sort and merge per kind, a review cycle with one finding, refile, assemble --check, assemble. The deltas-only path works: the assembled discovery listed 2 promise changes and wrote nothing under .ok-planner/design/. Then, in a copy of that scratch project, I had the story merge record a question instead of a new delta, because the README and the code disagree (the survey prompt, core.md:105, says 'Where prose and code in your area disagree, record the candidate once and say both in its body'). The question used artifact=story:read-balance, stale_op=new, stale_target=story:read-balance, and its answer body sat at answers/void-counting/stories/read-balance.md. The assembly refused it: 'the discovery does not hold: - question void-counting (item i14, task t16): artifact story:read-balance does not exist', exit 2. question_failures in scripts/discover (lines 455-459) requires the question's artifact to be a live file. So on an empty corpus the audit cannot ask any question, and a disagreement the code does not settle can only be dropped or quietly decided as a new delta. That contradicts the review prompt, core.md:513-515: 'Every promise change says what in the code settles it, and the code says it. A promise change the code does not settle is a question.' On an empty corpus every promise change is a new delta, so a reviewer following that line produces a finding that the merge cannot record in a form the assembly accepts. The same gap hits any new artifact on an out-of-date corpus; see the out-of-date failure. The story promises: 'have my existing code read against my design corpus, whether the corpus is empty or out of date, and turned into the corpus changes it needs plus the questions only I can answer'. The decision corpus-audit-hands-a-discovery-to-planning promises: 'It drafts each corpus delta the code and the rules settle, and each question only the owner can answer, with both answers'. Saw: on an empty corpus a discovery can carry deltas and calls but no question. Evidence: the assemble --check output quoted above.

Ran /discover-design's steps by hand in a scratch copy holding an out-of-date corpus: concept ledger-entry with a ## History section, and story read-balance, which says voided entries are counted while app/ledger.py skips them. The steps were survey, check (artifacts batched by kind), sort and merge per kind, review, and assemble. The main path holds: the discovery listed one form-only amendment (the History section stripped) and one question with both answers (stale: amend story:read-balance, body under answers/void-counting/; wrong: make balance count voided entries). Nothing under .ok-planner/design/ changed. The gap: the merge prompt, core.md:370, says 'A group under a proposed slug is a gap: where the definitions admit it, it becomes a new delta, marked promise'. That gives a gap only two exits, a new delta or a drop. The review prompt, core.md:513-515, says 'A promise change the code does not settle is a question'. But the assembly's question_failures (scripts/discover:455-459) refuses a question whose artifact is not a live file: 'artifact <kind:slug> does not exist'. So where the code holds something no artifact records (one of the three ways DISCOVER-FINDING-FORMS says a corpus is out of date) and the code and its prose disagree on what it should do, the audit cannot ask the owner. It must decide in a new delta or drop the candidate. This is the same root cause as the empty-corpus failure, here limited to new artifacts. The story promises: 'turned into the corpus changes it needs plus the questions only I can answer'. Saw: questions are possible only on live artifacts. Evidence: the refusal quoted in the empty-corpus failure, which was reproduced with stale_op=new.

body: What I did, in order: in a scratch project (stack run run-0a5e9cb47566, git init), ran true-up (exit 0), resolve citation-tags, wire-hooks lint (wired: PostToolUse matcher "" running node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.ok-planner/hooks/post-edit.js"), committed a base, then fed the wired command Claude Code PostToolUse payloads. Edit, Write, and MultiEdit payloads are checked as promised: a prose comment blocks (exit 2, 'plumbline/comment-hygiene: comment is not permitted'), a test file blocks ('plumbline/no-tests'), an unresolved @practice: slug blocks ('plumbline/citation-unresolved'), legacy debt on unchanged lines of a tracked file passes, each lint_checks switch turned off stops its check and true-up drops the matching rule text, and a declared folder beside the root is checked. Then the gap: an agent edit made through the Bash tool is never checked. With src/edit-time-lint-bash.js holding 'export const y = 2; // bash-written residue' on disk, a realistic Bash payload {tool_name:Bash, tool_input:{command:'printf ... > src/edit-time-lint-bash.js'}} gave 'hook exit=0' and no output, while the same file under a Write payload gave exit 2 with the comment-hygiene violation. A NotebookEdit payload on src/edit-time-lint.ipynb whose cell holds '# this sets x to one' also gave 'hook exit=0', and 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/edit-time-lint.ipynb' exits 0 on it, so notebook edits land unchecked too. The story promises: 'every agent edit checked against the lint checks my project turned on as it lands, so that residue never accumulates.' Saw: only edits through the Edit/Write/MultiEdit tools are checked; an agent that edits with sed -i, a heredoc, a redirect, or a script through Bash (which Claude Code's auto mode tells agents they may do for small edits) lands residue the hook never sees, and it accumulates until a whole-tree lint run. The product says so itself: .claude/rules/plumbline-cheatsheet.md, 'It does nothing for a Bash call.', and decision edit-hook-blocks-in-turn scopes the hook to 'the edited file', so the fix may need the owner's ruling (for example, lint the files git reports changed after a Bash call). Side observation, same hook: the hook also lints on a Read payload, so reading an untracked file that holds a comment gives exit 2 ('src/edit-time-lint-bash.js:1: plumbline/comment-hygiene') on a file the agent did not edit. Evidence: 'hook exit=0' for the Bash and NotebookEdit payloads above; 'hook exit=2' for the Write and Read payloads on the same file.
note: two readings: the story owes a check of every edit an agent makes, through Bash (sed -i, a redirect, a script) or NotebookEdit too; the story owes a check of the edits the post-edit hook sees, the Edit/Write/MultiEdit tools' edited file; the first rests on story:edit-time-lint-enforcement 'every agent edit checked against the lint checks my project turned on as it lands', the second on decision:edit-hook-blocks-in-turn's Choice 'a post-edit hook ... within the edited file's changed line ranges' and the rules text 'It does nothing for a Bash call.'

Reading 1: 'every agent edit checked ... as it lands' (story:edit-time-lint-enforcement) covers edits through any tool, so the hook owes a check after Bash and NotebookEdit calls, e.g. over the files git reports changed. Reading 2: decision:edit-hook-blocks-in-turn's Choice, 'a post-edit hook ... within the edited file's changed line ranges', with the rules text 'It does nothing for a Bash call.', scopes the check to the editing tools' named file, and Bash edits are left to a whole-tree lint.

In a scratch project with docspec 'guide' stamped by a documentation sprint over docs/guide.md, I deleted .ok-planner/docspec/guide.md, as a sprint's '### Retire docspec: guide' delta does, regenerated the index, and committed. Saw: 'docs window' printed 'no docspec under .ok-planner/docspec: the project declares no documentation' (exit 0). docs/guide.md and .ok-planner/doc-state/guide.json both stayed tracked. /plan-docs SKILL.md step 1 says 'Where .ok-planner/docspec/ is missing or holds no docspec ... say that /plan-sprint declares a docspec, and stop.' The sprint build prompt (skills/_sprint/shared.md) tells builders to 'Leave every file under the ## Where of a docspec ... as it stands', so the retiring sprint does not remove the files either. Nothing in the suite ever drops or checks them again. The same applies when an Amend docspec delta moves '## Where': the DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT in core.md reads only 'files under the docspec's ## Where as they stand' (step 1, 'Per file under the Where'), and a 'drop' is only 'a file the layout no longer calls for' under that Where, so the files at the old path are left behind. The story promises: after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands. In both cases stale documentation stays in the tree, outside every window, describing a product that has moved on.
note: two readings: the story owes that documentation left under a retired docspec, or under a docspec's old ## Where after an Amend moves it, is dropped or checked by a documentation sprint; the story covers only the documents a live docspec declares, and the sprint that retires or moves a docspec decides the old files; the first rests on story:keep-documentation-current 'after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands', the second on its 'bring every document my project keeps up to date' with decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window, which plans only docspecs that exist.

Reading 1: story:keep-documentation-current, 'after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands', owes that a documentation sprint drops or checks those orphaned files. Reading 2: the story's 'every document my project keeps' and decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window, which plans each docspec that exists, cover only documents a live docspec declares, and the sprint that retires or moves the docspec owns the old files' fate.

- i52: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:archive_show. - i50: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:backlog_entry. The widened path pattern (review:1027, PATH_ALTERNATIVES = r'[\w.-]*(?:/[\w.-]+)+|[\w./-]+\.\w+') matches absolute extensionless paths such as /usr/bin/env, /bin/sh, or /etc/services. backlog_entry tests os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, token)) (review:1078), and os.path.join with an absolute token returns the token, so a system file passes; left_alone finds no owner path, harness match, or stamp, so the token lands in files (review:1084 files.append(token)). Trigger: an open category: defect issue whose problem names such a path (a shebang, or /etc/services, which project.md itself names). Harm: review backlog reports a file outside the project tree as a file of the tree, as the issue's site and in files, which reach the fix task's --files as a file the run may edit (A9; the A2 write target follows where a fixer acts on it). Scope: caused by the change; the base PATH_PATTERN r'[\w./-]+\.\w+' (base review:1014) required an extension, and B9 widens the match only for files of the tree. From report i15.

The new catch 'except ReviewError as err: return str(err)' (review:1698-1699) stands, since certification_failures acts on the reason it returns, but it emits no event and does not re-raise. Rule: .ok-planner/docs/events.md, Where the code emits: 'every error caught: a catch that stands under the Errors section ... emits on the caught path', and 'A caught error that neither emits nor re-raises is a defect.' The one compliant form is an emission through the project's event helper (issues.tasks.event, as main does at review:1930) on the caught path. Trigger: review certified --sprint <path> on a project with a story whose ## Drive commands section is missing, holds a - No stack: line beside a stack line, or whose stack-start line is refused; drive_stack or drive_command raises ReviewError and the catch swallows it with no record. Scope: caused by the change; at the base the only ReviewError catch was main's owner frame. From report i16.

What the code does: for a sprint with no approval mark and no base file, cmd_certified passes approval_refusal's message to certified_verdict as its one failure (scripts/review:1741-1743 'if refusal: return certified_verdict(sprint, [refusal])'), and certified_verdict prints, after the failure, 'The completion contract does not hold yet. Keep working toward the goal for this sprint file.' (scripts/review:1763). Harm (A9): the command's last line tells the session and the /goal checker, which reads only that output, to keep working on a draft the owner never approved, the opposite of decision sprints-carry-an-approval-mark ('Every executor of a sprint refuses to execute one that carries no mark ... the command that checks the completion contract') and of the sprint's step 2, which stops. In scope: sprint work item 15 added approval_refusal and its route through certified_verdict in cmd_certified. Evidence: driver's scratch run printed 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE: ...-draft.md' / '- ... carries no approval mark, so it may be a draft the owner never approved; if you approved it, add approved: <date> ...' / 'The completion contract does not hold yet. Keep working toward the goal for this sprint file.', exit 2. Failure: i29.
- i66: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:confirm_briefs (with drive_names and cmd_drives), and the merge prompt's rule at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/merge.md:46. What the code does: merge.md:46 directs 'Two failures with one cause are one defect naming both stories.' but gives only '--field story=<slug>' and no form for two stories. confirm_briefs uses fields['story'] whole as the brief's story, and drive_names builds '<story>-<digest>' and raises ReviewError when the name does not match [a-z0-9-]+ (' rename its story'). Scope: archive_show and uncommitted stood at the base, but B114 newly routes stale tracked suite files in a no-HEAD repository through this Show, so the change newly exposes /ok's consent to it. From report i18.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:archive_show. body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:backlog_entry. The widened path pattern (review:1027, PATH_ALTERNATIVES = r'[\w.-]*(?:/[\w.-]+)+|[\w./-]+\.\w+') matches absolute extensionless paths such as /usr/bin/env, /bin/sh, or /etc/services. backlog_entry tests os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, token)) (review:1078), and os.path.join with an absolute token returns the token, so a system file passes; left_alone finds no owner path, harness match, or stamp, so the token lands in files (review:1084 files.append(token)). Trigger: an open category: defect issue whose problem names such a path (a shebang, or /etc/services, which project.md itself names). Harm: review backlog reports a file outside the project tree as a file of the tree, as the issue's site and in files, which reach the fix task's --files as a file the run may edit (A9; the A2 write target follows where a fixer acts on it). Scope: caused by the change; the base PATH_PATTERN r'[\w./-]+\.\w+' (base review:1014) required an extension, and B9 widens the match only for files of the tree. From report i15.
note: review:backlog_entry now skips a token that is an absolute path or whose normalized form starts with '..' before the isfile test, so /usr/bin/env, /bin/sh, /etc/services, or ../x never reach files or site; a token of the tree passes as before. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review. Sites enumerated: PATH_PATTERN and SITE_PATTERN are read only in backlog_entry (review:1077, :1088).

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:undriven_reason. The new catch 'except ReviewError as err: return str(err)' (review:1698-1699) stands, since certification_failures acts on the reason it returns, but it emits no event and does not re-raise. Rule: .ok-planner/docs/events.md, Where the code emits: 'every error caught: a catch that stands under the Errors section ... emits on the caught path', and 'A caught error that neither emits nor re-raises is a defect.' The one compliant form is an emission through the project's event helper (issues.tasks.event, as main does at review:1930) on the caught path. Harm: /ok step 4 shows the owner the output of each Show: command before the one consent question, and every Show under these steps prints a git error instead of the content the step archives and overwrites, so the owner consents without seeing the work at stake and the error does not say why (A3). ADMINISTRATION.md:44 documents this exact Show for the no-commit case. Scope: archive_show and uncommitted stood at the base, but B114 newly routes stale tracked suite files in a no-HEAD repository through this Show, so the change newly exposes /ok's consent to it. From report i18.
note: Checked true-up diff: no_commit() factors the HEAD rev-parse check uncommitted() made; archive_show returns git diff HEAD only where paths are uncommitted and HEAD exists, else cat -- of the files. Every caller (copy_step:4294, materialize_steps stale step:4059, archive_step:3613, move_step:3638, folder_show:4179) now prints the working file in a no-commit repo instead of 'fatal: bad revision HEAD'; committed-repo and non-git paths unchanged. body: Reviewed /converge (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, prompts/fix.md, verify.md, owner-list.md, scripts/review fixes/verifies/drives, scripts/tasks close) for the whole variant: find each break by a drive, then fix it or report it. Then ran the loop's verbs in a scratch project (stack run run-fcb308601e42, trued up from the working tree): one drive failure merged as defect i2, review fixes --round 1 filed fix task t4 with --mark fixing, the fixer closed t4 'done' (--staged tool.sh --sites tool.sh) without running tasks item set on i2. The story promises: each break the check finds is fixed, so a change that breaks a promise does not reach users unnoticed. Saw: tasks close accepts a done close of a batch fix task whose defect still stands 'fixing' (cmd_close checks only swept-role --sites); i2 stayed 'fixing'; review verifies --snapshot fix-1.json printed {"verify_tasks": []} because cmd_verifies takes only fixed/declined/duplicate; tasks item list --state open printed []; review drives --confirm --dry-run printed {"pending": []}. So Loop 2 step 2 ('Where no defect stands at open, the loop ends') ends the loop with the break neither fixed nor verified. SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 resets defects 'still fixing' only after a partial/blocked/disputed close ('A fix task that closes blocked or disputed, or partial with any other result, is refiled once ... its defects still fixing go back to open'), never after a done close. owner-list.md reads only 'the defects stuck, the defects still open or fixed where the run ended before they were verified, the defects at declined or duplicate with no verified field' and never names 'fixing', and the return's 'fixed' line counts verified, declined, duplicate, and stuck. The found break therefore reaches neither the fix loop, the intake, nor the report: it goes unnoticed, against the story's 'have each break that check finds fixed, so that a change that breaks a promise does not reach my users unnoticed' and decision converge-finds-then-fixes ('Every defect on the list is fixed in the run, declined with a reason a verifier accepts, or stuck', SKILL.md 'The intent is to fix, not to file').
note: fix-task-closed-done-leaves-defect-fixing

body: Reviewed /plan-docs (skills/plan-docs/SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) and drove .ok-planner/bin/docs in a scratch project. A docspec's ## Reader and ## Covers (whom the documentation is for, what it tells and leaves out) never cause an edit. {{DOC-EDIT-RULES}} in core.md lists six rules (false claim, missing public element, internal element shown, a closed sprint changed what a user can do through the references, departure from ## Shape or the ## Where layout, unsettleable claim) and then says 'Every other sentence stays as written.' No rule fires when the documentation's reader or coverage departs from ## Reader or ## Covers. Scratch drive: stamped docspec:guides over docs/guides/greet-someone.md, then amended its Reader to 'A person new to the command line who has never run a Python script.' and its Covers to add 'how to install Python first', committed. 'docs window --json' gave status reached, reasons ['docspec changed: .ok-planner/docspec/guides.md'], sprints [], stale_claims 0. Under {{DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT}} steps 1-2 no rule fires and the file is neither changed nor checked ('Any other file is not an item'), so plan-docs step 5 writes 'No item: nothing its reader sees changed.' and the stamp moves past the amendment: the owner's new reader and coverage are never written. The same holds when a docspec is first declared over existing documentation (planner step 3: existing files are change or check 'under the steps above'), so existing text that covers what Covers leaves out, or omits what it names, stays. The style pass also may 'add no claim, and cut none' and revises against Shape, example, and writing standard only. The story promises: 'declare each kind of documentation my project keeps, whom it is for, and what it describes, so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; concept:docspec Purpose: 'The docspec also tells the writer whom the text is for, what to cover, what to leave out ... so the text follows the owner's intent instead of the writer's guess.'; decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window: 'Planning takes each docspec whose own text ... changed since its stamp'. Saw: the window takes the changed docspec text, but no edit rule acts on it.
note: doc-edit-rules-ignore-reader-and-covers

Its Judge step then rests on fields that output never prints: 'A message carrying edited is one you answered before, which its author has since rewritten; its earlier field holds the texts you answered, so answer what changed. I seeded docspec 'guide' (Where docs/guide.md, References src/cli.py; no stamp, so it was planned as new), wrote a documentation sprint with one 'change' item, ran the boilerplate's steps 3-5 (base, tasks init, prompts, item_states, one write task closed done) and step 6 (one style task closed done), skipped step 7's fact loop entirely, and wrote the report. The story promises: after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands. decision:documentation-claims-checked-until-they-hold says 'a checker that is not the writer checks each claim the run must check ... until every claim holds or is cut', and decision:documentation-claim-ledger says a docspec planned as new has every claim in every file checked. Saw: '.ok-planner/bin/docs complete' printed 'DOCS COMPLETE: .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-10-22-guide.md / The completion contract holds. This meets the goal for this documentation sprint.' (exit 0), and the report said '0 held: 0 by run, 0 by ask, 0 by read, 0 by link.' 'docs stamp' then wrote '0 claims in its ledger', and the next window reported the docspec 'current'. Cause: scripts/docs complete_failures (line 531) requires a write task per write/change/drop item and a style task per changed file, but no checker task and no recorded claim for any planned file. The completion contract in skills/plan-docs/doc-sprint-document.md item 1 has the same gap. Under /goal the checker decides from this command's output alone, so a run that skips the fact loop meets the goal with unchecked claims, and the empty ledger means the next run never checks those claims either.

body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's issue walk, the step where the owner settles a coverage gap or collision (the judgment issues by which a missing or conflicting practice gets recorded). In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (stack run run-a3e2818f77e6), I authored subject rcp-cli-commands and practices rcp-commands-return-exit-codes and rcp-streaming-commands-exit, filed issue rcp-gap-async-commands with artifacts ["subject:rcp-cli-commands", "practice:rcp-commands-return-exit-codes", "practice:rcp-streaming-commands-exit"], and ran the walk's command 'OK_PLANNER_PROJECT_ROOT=<project> python3 .ok-planner/scripts/surface-corpus rcp-gap-async-commands'. The story promises: the policies a codebase follows are recorded as citable artifacts naming the population and condition, so an agent can tell which policy accounts for a construct; plan-sprint SKILL.md line 142 sends gaps and collisions to the intake to be walked like any other issue, and artifact-definitions.md says ' takes , , , , , and  slugs'. Saw: surface-corpus printed nothing, exit 0, with and without a design/ folder present. The script only knows FOLDERS = {"concept": "concepts", "story": "stories", "decision": "decisions"}, skips any artifact whose kind is not in FOLDERS ('if kind not in FOLDERS: continue'), gathers only .ok-planner/design/, and returns early with no output when design/ holds nothing ('if not docs: return 0'). SKILL.md line 153 then tells the walker: 'Where the script prints nothing, the issue is either about pure code with no corpus commitment or about a concept the record failed to name: flag it to the owner.' So a gap or collision issue that names its subject and practices is walked with none of them surfaced, and is misreported to the owner as having no corpus bearing. evidence: 'filed rcp-gap-async-commands / file exit 0 / surface exit 0' with empty output in both runs.

body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's Sign-off step and the compliance reviewer prompt it dispatches. SKILL.md step 7 (line 175) says: 'Walk with the owner only a judgment finding that meets {{OWNER-QUESTION-TEST}}; settle every other one as a call the rules decide, and list it at Approval. Re-dispatch until clean.' The reviewer prompt in skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md has only a [REVIEW SCOPE] slot. It has no slot for findings the owner already settled (the implementation notes review has one, [SETTLED], core.md line 415). So when the owner answers a judgment finding by keeping the flagged text (for example, the existence-test question 'the owner retires the concept or names the neighbor it merges into', where the owner keeps the concept), or when the session settles a finding as a call that keeps the text, the next dispatch flags it again. 'Until clean' then ends only once the session rewrites the text against the owner's answer, or never ends. The story promises: a signed-off sprint reached 'without ... deciding my open questions for me'. Saw: the text gives the session no path to a clean review that keeps an owner's answer, short of overriding that answer. Evidence: SKILL.md:175 'Re-dispatch until clean.'; design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md:35 'Replace [REVIEW SCOPE]; everything else is invariant.'; core.md:415 'Settled by the owner, and not raised again: [SETTLED].' That is false when the start failed because another live verification run in the same checkout holds the fixed name drive: the second run's stop line then takes down the first run's live stack and releases its leased ports, which the registry can lease to a later run while the first run's drivers still address them. The story promises: each verification run builds and resolves its own artifacts, so no run can pick up another run's (concept run-tag: 'Concurrent runs cannot collide on an artifact or on a stack'). Saw: first run 'stack up --name drive' -> 'run-cfc94a3e1f1b / WEB_PORT=44856', exit 0; second run's start -> 'stack: the run run-cfc94a3e1f1b holds the name drive, and 1 running container(s) carry its label or belong to its compose project; stack down --name drive takes it down', exit 1; second run's stop line -> 'took down: run-cfc94a3e1f1b (WEB_PORT=44856; 1 container(s), 1 network(s), 0 volume(s), 1 image(s))', exit 0; first run's verify by its own tag -> 'no artifact carries tag run-cfc94a3e1f1b', exit 1. The stop line keys on the shared name, not on the tag the run's own start minted, so one run's teardown reaches another run's stack.

A foreign program holding a leased port made up retry with a fresh tag (STACK.START.RETRIED attempt 2) and succeed. Two docker-backed runs: down of one swept its network and volume and left the other's. All of that achieved the benefit. Then docker's daemon hung for a few minutes on this machine (docker ps -q still hanging after 8s; another driver's 'docker ps -a -q --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=run-be8ad7b2f2c4' hung too). During that window '.ok-planner/bin/stack up --name drive' sat for over 2.5 minutes with the run entry recorded as 'no ports' and no run folder, its child '/usr/local/bin/docker ps -a -q' hung, until I killed it (exit 143). A separate '.ok-planner/bin/ports lease run-b27174a2f8e5' for a fresh tag also never returned, killed by a 20 s alarm (rc 142). body: Reviewed /plan-tests (SKILL.md step 5.2, core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT, TEST-LEGACY-PROMPT, TEST-SWEEP-PROMPT, TEST-FIX-PROMPT) and scripts/tests (assembled_plan, plan_failures, stage_write, live_tests, stray_paths). The sort decides fixtures before it can know which tests are adopted, and no later step corrects that decision. SKILL.md step 5.2 files 'one sort task per ten of them, in path order', and the drain runs those tasks side by side. A fixture under tests/fixtures/ usually sits in a different batch from the tests that read it. The sort table says: 'It is a fixture or a helper that an adopted test uses. | support, naming the scenarios it serves'. An agent sorting the fixture's batch cannot see the adopt decisions another batch has not yet made. Nothing after the sort reconciles fixtures with adopted tests: tests plan checks only that a support entry names planned scenarios ('support names a scenario the plan lacks'), the plan review checks only ports and adopts, and the sweep acts only on files no record claims. (1) A fixture an adopted test reads that gets sorted 'delete' is removed by its legacy task. The adopted test then fails, and TEST-FIX-PROMPT forbids the fix: 'you change no test: no file at a test path, no support file, no fixture'. The fix tasks close blocked twice and the run stops at a genuine blocker. The test that guarded a promise is lost. (2) A fixture sorted 'support' whose adopted test does not use it is claimed through legacy_support in live_tests, so stray_paths never lists it and the sweep never deletes it. Part of the old suite stays. The story promises: keep the tests that check what my product promises and drop the rest. decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'So is a fixture or a data file no kept test uses [deleted]'. Saw: no step bases the support or delete sort of a fixture on the final set of adopted tests. evidence: SKILL.md step 5.2 'file one sort task per ten of them, in path order'; core.md sort table row 'It is a fixture or a helper that an adopted test uses'; scripts/tests live_tests 'legacy_support = {e["path"] for e in plan["legacy"] if e["sort"] == "support" and s["id"] in e["scenarios"]}'.

body: Reviewed /plan-tests SKILL.md step 2 (the runner), core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT, and scripts/tests plan_failures and assembled_plan. The second scenario then gets a new test, and its legacy tests stay inside the adopted file as duplicates the plan never deletes. The story promises: drop the rest, so that the old suite does not block my changes. decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'sorts every test no scenario claims ... A test that checks the code against itself, or a behavior no story or rule names, is an orphan, and is deleted' and 'Where two legacy tests check one scenario, the first is adopted and the second deleted'. Saw: with a file-level runner the skill sorts files, not tests, and no step asks for a runner that addresses one test when a legacy suite is present. evidence: core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT 'each file otherwise'; scripts/tests locator() 'return "%s::%s" % (test["path"], test["name"]) if test.get("name") else test["path"]'.

body: What I did, in order: in a scratch project (stack run run-0a5e9cb47566, git init), ran true-up (exit 0), resolve citation-tags, wire-hooks lint (wired: PostToolUse matcher "" running node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.ok-planner/hooks/post-edit.js"), committed a base, then fed the wired command Claude Code PostToolUse payloads. Edit, Write, and MultiEdit payloads are checked as promised: a prose comment blocks (exit 2, 'plumbline/comment-hygiene: comment is not permitted'), a test file blocks ('plumbline/no-tests'), an unresolved @practice: slug blocks ('plumbline/citation-unresolved'), legacy debt on unchanged lines of a tracked file passes, each lint_checks switch turned off stops its check and true-up drops the matching rule text, and a declared folder beside the root is checked. Then the gap: an agent edit made through the Bash tool is never checked. With src/edit-time-lint-bash.js holding 'export const y = 2; // bash-written residue' on disk, a realistic Bash payload {tool_name:Bash, tool_input:{command:'printf ... > src/edit-time-lint-bash.js'}} gave 'hook exit=0' and no output, while the same file under a Write payload gave exit 2 with the comment-hygiene violation. A NotebookEdit payload on src/edit-time-lint.ipynb whose cell holds '# this sets x to one' also gave 'hook exit=0', and 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/edit-time-lint.ipynb' exits 0 on it, so notebook edits land unchecked too. The story promises: 'every agent edit checked against the lint checks my project turned on as it lands, so that residue never accumulates.' Saw: only edits through the Edit/Write/MultiEdit tools are checked; an agent that edits with sed -i, a heredoc, a redirect, or a script through Bash (which Claude Code's auto mode tells agents they may do for small edits) lands residue the hook never sees, and it accumulates until a whole-tree lint run. The product says so itself: .claude/rules/plumbline-cheatsheet.md, 'It does nothing for a Bash call.', and decision edit-hook-blocks-in-turn scopes the hook to 'the edited file', so the fix may need the owner's ruling (for example, lint the files git reports changed after a Bash call). Side observation, same hook: the hook also lints on a Read payload, so reading an untracked file that holds a comment gives exit 2 ('src/edit-time-lint-bash.js:1: plumbline/comment-hygiene') on a file the agent did not edit. Evidence: 'hook exit=0' for the Bash and NotebookEdit payloads above; 'hook exit=2' for the Write and Read payloads on the same file.
note: edit-hook-skips-bash-and-notebook-edits

body: What the product does: once a sprint retires a docspec, 'docs window' says the project declares no documentation (or skips it), and its files and doc-state stay tracked with nothing ever dropping or checking them; once an Amend moves a docspec's ## Where, the planner reads only files under the new Where, so files at the old path stay (driver t12, failure i21; scripts/docs, skills/plan-docs/core.md, skills/_sprint/shared.md 'Leave every file under the ## Where ... as it stands'). Reading 1: story:keep-documentation-current, 'after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands', owes that a documentation sprint drops or checks those orphaned files. Reading 2: the story's 'every document my project keeps' and decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window, which plans each docspec that exists, cover only documents a live docspec declares, and the sprint that retires or moves the docspec owns the old files' fate.
note: retired-docspec-leaves-documentation-behind

body: In a scratch project with docspec 'guide' stamped by a documentation sprint over docs/guide.md, I deleted .ok-planner/docspec/guide.md, as a sprint's '### Retire docspec: guide' delta does, regenerated the index, and committed. Saw: 'docs window' printed 'no docspec under .ok-planner/docspec: the project declares no documentation' (exit 0). docs/guide.md and .ok-planner/doc-state/guide.json both stayed tracked. /plan-docs SKILL.md step 1 says 'Where .ok-planner/docspec/ is missing or holds no docspec ... say that /plan-sprint declares a docspec, and stop.' The sprint build prompt (skills/_sprint/shared.md) tells builders to 'Leave every file under the ## Where of a docspec ... as it stands', so the retiring sprint does not remove the files either. Nothing in the suite ever drops or checks them again. The same applies when an Amend docspec delta moves '## Where': the DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT in core.md reads only 'files under the docspec's ## Where as they stand' (step 1, 'Per file under the Where'), and a 'drop' is only 'a file the layout no longer calls for' under that Where, so the files at the old path are left behind. The story promises: after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands. In both cases stale documentation stays in the tree, outside every window, describing a product that has moved on.
note: retired-docspec-leaves-documentation-behind

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:inline_body. What the code does: it opens a delta's inline body at the first line matching '^(`{3,})markdown' and ends it at the first later line equal to that same fence (scripts/review:1563-1569), so a final-form body that holds its own ``` code block, fenced with ```markdown, is cut at its first inner fence. Neither the delta form ({{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}}, skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:284) nor the sprint template (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:30-39) says how to fence a body that holds a code block. Trigger: a delta '### New decision: cc-fenced' whose ```markdown body holds '```' / 'make check' / '```', landed byte for byte. Harm (A9): review deltas (cmd_deltas, a path this change added, item 13) lists the landed delta as unsettled ('cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body'), and review certified prints 'item 1 (deltas): fails' and SPRINT NOT COMPLETE over a delta that landed as approved; a C3 fixer that copies the body verbatim cannot clear it. Evidence: driver t5's scratch run, 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE ... - New decision: cc-fenced: .ok-planner/design/decisions/cc-fenced.md differs from the delta's body' (failures i11, i12).
note: delta-body-inner-fence-breaks-certification

body: scripts/review:fence_depths; how the delta tools read a backtick line with an info string inside an open fence; readings: CommonMark (it is content, so a three-backtick body holding a '```sh' block closes at that block's bare closer and the delta form's more-backticks rule must be followed), or nested (it opens an inner fence that its own bare closer ends); built nested, so a body that breaks the form still reads as its author wrote it and no later delta heading drops out of the count
